nodes.notes: No Navigation component; activities + manual fragment transactions. RecordingActivity uses a dark translucent theme (MANIFEST:57-60).

nodes.behavior: RecordingStore persists two things. (1) SharedPreferences file 'plaud_template_prefs' (MODE_PRIVATE) with keys: last_connected_device_sn (String, doubles as activeDeviceSN), paired_device_sns (Gson JSON array String), paired_device_names (Gson JSON map SN->name), user_id, is_auto_sync_enabled (default TRUE), fast_transfer_never_show, user_access_token_override, api_key_override, server_domain_override, has_skipped_onboarding. (2) filesDir/recordings.json: a Gson List<RecordingFile> rewritten in full on every mutation (add/delete/rename/updateDuration/updateTranscript/markAsSynced/replaceAllFiles) under a JVM lock. No SQLite/Room, no EncryptedSharedPreferences, no encryption at rest in the app.
nodes.notes: The token override is stored in plain SharedPreferences (RecordingStore.kt:84-86). allFiles is sorted createdAt-desc on every read (153-156).

nodes.behavior: RecordingFile schema (Gson @SerializedName): id (UUID string, app-generated), sessionId (Long, device session id = epoch seconds), deviceSN, name (default 'Untitled Recording'), duration (seconds), createdAt (ms = sessionId*1000), syncedAt (ms or null), localPath (absolute path or null), summaryText (never written by any code path), transcriptJSON (raw results array string). isSynced := localPath != null. addFiles dedupes by sessionId, delete/rename/updateTranscript key by id, markAsSynced keys by sessionId.
nodes.notes: sessionId is the cross-layer identifier (device file id == BLE sessionId == createdAt source). No cloud id is ever stored for a recording.

nodes.behavior: Synced audio lives in cacheDir/export (RecordingStore.exportDir), not in filesDir: both BLE exportAudio and Wi-Fi exportAudioViaWiFi are given outputDir = exportDir, format MP3, channels 1; the SDK chooses the file name (outputFile.name is only logged) and localPath is set to outputFile.absolutePath. RecordingStore.audioFilePath() (filesDir/audio/<sessionId>.opus) and clearAll() (which wipes filesDir/audio and all prefs) have no callers. FileProvider exposes both cache and files roots for sharing.
nodes.evidence: T/storage/RecordingStore.kt:224-244; T/managers/SyncManager.kt:391-400,418-420,595-600,785-792,746-749; RES/xml/file_paths.xml:3-5; grep: no callers of audioFilePath/clearAll outside their definition
nodes.notes: Consequence (INFERRED): Android may evict cacheDir under storage pressure, leaving recordings.json rows with isSynced=true but a missing file; FileDetail then hides the player (FileDetailActivity.kt:298-305) and transcription fails 'Audio file not found' (TranscriptionManager.kt:92-95). Since the device copy was deleted after sync, the audio is then unrecoverable from the app's point of view.

nodes.behavior: What survives reinstall: android:allowBackup="true" with no backup rules, so prefs and filesDir/recordings.json are eligible for Android auto-backup/restore; cacheDir (the audio) is never backed up. Nothing else (no cloud sync of the library: the app never lists or fetches recordings/transcripts from the cloud). Sign-out/unpair does NOT clear recordings.json or audio (clearAll is unreachable); the code comment says synced recordings intentionally survive.
nodes.evidence: MANIFEST:21-29; T/ui/settings/SettingsFragment.kt:292-300; T/storage/RecordingStore.kt:237-244 (no callers); T/managers/SyncManager.kt:575-579 (reset clears only in-memory list)
nodes.notes: WelcomeActivity.kt:52-53 comment 'the built-in token expired after a reinstall' implies Plaud QA observed the build-time token, not the override, being active after reinstall.

nodes.behavior: Recording state machine: sealed RecordingState { Idle, Recording(sessionId, startedAt), Paused(sessionId) }. Commands go to the facade: startRecord(scene=0), stopRecord(scene=0), pauseRecord(sid,0), resumeRecord(sid,0). State changes ONLY from device callbacks bleRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume forwarded by DeviceManager to RecordingManager.handle*. startedAt = sessionId*1000 (sessionId>0) else startTime*1000 else now. Drift protection: 1.5 s after start/stop, if the state is not as expected call refreshRecordState(); refreshRecordState() also on every connect and on RecordingActivity.onResume; bleRecordStateRefreshed(isRecording, sessionId) forces Recording or Idle. On stop the app waits 1 s then startSync() if isAutoSyncEnabled else fetchFileList(). UI shows 'Starting...' with a 4 s ack timeout; the main button stops and closes the screen; pause/resume live on a side button.
nodes.notes: Device is the source of truth for recording state; the app never assumes success on command send. The facade blePenState carries no sessionId (DeviceManager.kt:374-378), which is why refreshRecordState exists.

nodes.behavior: Waveform is not driven on Android: RecordingManager.handlePcmData (RMS*3 clamp) exists but has no caller; DeviceManager's PlaudDeviceAgentListener implements no blePcmData; javap ALL.txt contains no blePcmData symbol. The 100 ms waveform timer therefore publishes latestLevel=0 and WaveformView draws minimum-height bars.
nodes.evidence: T/managers/RecordingManager.kt:166-199; T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:213-411 (listener overrides); build/evidence/javap/ALL.txt (grep blePcmData: no hits); T/ui/recording/RecordingActivity.kt:212-262
nodes.notes: README claims 'Real-time recording with live PCM waveform' for both platforms; iOS has blePcmData/JXRecordVolumer (README 'Recording & Waveform'), Android does not.

nodes.behavior: Sync state machine: SyncState { Idle, Syncing(progress), WiFiConnecting(OPENING_HOTSPOT|CONNECTING_WIFI|HANDSHAKING), WiFiTransferring(progress), Completed, Failed(msg) }; SyncProgress { totalFiles, syncedFiles, currentFileName, fileProgress 0..1, bytesPerSecond } with progressFraction=(synced+fileProgress)/total. BLE path: startSync() (ignored if active) -> PlaudDeviceAgent.getFileList() -> bleFileList -> handleFileList: durations are forced to 0 (BleFile exposes no public duration), deviceSN = lastConnectedDeviceSN; recordings.json is REPLACED with (local rows where isSynced) + (device sessionIds not in that set, as new unsynced rows) -> if silentFetch: Idle; else if no new: Completed; else sequential downloadNextFile(). Download = exportAudio(sessionId, cacheDir/export, MP3, 1ch); onProgress feeds a speed estimate (ignores samples <0.1 s apart); onStageChanged records ExportStage; onComplete -> OpusRepair.repairIfNeeded (no-op on MP3), markAsSynced(sessionId, path, duration measured from the file), deleteFile(sessionId) on device, next; onError -> log, syncedCount++, next (no retry).
nodes.notes: Because handleFileList rebuilds the store from the device list, any unsynced local row for a file no longer on the device silently disappears, and an unsynced row's deviceSN is whatever device is active at fetch time. Duration is 0 until download; FileDetail self-heals 0 durations from the local file (FileDetailActivity.kt:87-101).

nodes.behavior: Auto-download-on-connect is NOT implemented on Android despite README/settings copy: onDeviceConnected schedules fetchFileList() after 3 s (skipped if recording), and fetchFileList sets silentFetch=true so handleFileList ends in Idle without downloading. The only automatic download trigger is RecordingManager.handleRecordStop -> 1 s -> startSync() when is_auto_sync_enabled (default true). Manual triggers: none in the UI for BLE sync except the post-recording path (there is no 'Sync now' button); the sync banner's only button is Fast Transfer.
nodes.notes: README 'File Sync | BLE sync with auto-download on connect' is refuted for the Android source; the settings subtitle 'Auto transfer recordings via BLE when device is connected' is inaccurate for this code.

nodes.behavior: Delete-after-sync policy is hardcoded and unconditional: BLE path calls PlaudDeviceAgent.deleteFile(sessionId) immediately after markAsSynced, result (bleDeleteFile status) is only logged; Wi-Fi path defers to one batched getWifiAgent().deleteFiles(list) after the export queue drains, waits up to 15 s (DELETE_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_MS) for onFileDeleteCompleted, then waits up to 20 s for the device to close the session itself. User-facing delete is local-only ('mirrors iOS'): removes the row and the local file, never touches the device. A synced file whose device delete failed is filtered out of future syncs (already in localSyncedIds) and is never re-deleted by the app.
nodes.notes: The comment at SyncManager.kt:751 says this mirrors iOS 'to avoid re-downloading'.

nodes.behavior: Wi-Fi fast transfer flow: entry from the sync banner button (Home or Files); FastTransferSheet shown unless fast_transfer_never_show; sheet text promises '10x' and that the phone temporarily joins the device hotspot. startWiFiTransfer(): re-entry guarded by wifiTransferActive; if a BLE export is in ExportStage.TRANSCODING it defers (wifiRequestedDuringExport) and resumes after that export; else stopSyncFile(), clear pending BLE queue, DeviceManager.suppressAutoReconnect=true, state WiFiConnecting(OPENING_HOTSPOT), 1.5 s DEVICE_IDLE_GRACE, then PlaudDeviceAgent.startWifiTransfer(userId, cb). Phases from onConnectionStateChanged: CONNECTING->CONNECTING_WIFI, CONNECTED/HANDSHAKING->HANDSHAKING; on READY or onHandshakeCompleted the app must explicitly call getWifiAgent().getFileList() (otherwise the device 'just heartbeats and closes'). onFileListReceived: registerWifiFiles (rows with deviceSN='' , duration from wf.duration/1000, createdAt from wf.timestamp*1000 else sessionId*1000), then serial exportAudioViaWiFi(MP3,1ch) per session (the raw downloadAllFiles path is avoided because it writes undecrypted, unplayable .opus). Empty list -> wait for device close. After the queue: batch delete, close-wait, finishWiFiTransfer: state final, NiceBuildSdk.stopWifiTransfer() (also asks the device over BLE to close the hotspot), on Failed+BLE-up additionally setDeviceWiFi(false); if BLE is down set DeviceManager.pendingDeviceWiFiClose so the next BLE connect sends setDeviceWiFi(false); suppressAutoReconnect=false; 1.5 s; attemptReconnect(). Speed shown is SDK-reported KB/s retained between samples.
nodes.notes: Comments encode device behaviour as observed by Plaud engineers (LINEAGE-grade claims): device refuses openWiFi with status 4 while streaming, connect fails 1003, device keeps hotspot ~2 min on firmware timeout, blue LED in Wi-Fi mode, flash erase takes several seconds (PLA2-309). The 'tap Join when prompted' string implies an Android system Wi-Fi join dialog, i.e. the SDK uses a user-consented network request; the mechanism is inside the SDK (UNKNOWN here).

nodes.behavior: Device connection state machine and multi-device model: DeviceConnectionState { Disconnected, Scanning, Connecting(device), Connected, Failed(msg) }. Scan results are filtered to SN prefixes 881 (NotePro) and 882 (NotePin S) only, sorted by RSSI desc, names sanitised (control chars dropped, fallback model name). connect(): waits up to 10 s for NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() (RSA gen-key), calls NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(type, sn), then PlaudDeviceAgent.connectBleDevice(bleDevice); success is declared ONLY on bleBind(status=0) (awaitingHandshake), GATT state 1 alone is ignored; state 0 or 2 while awaiting -> onHandshakeRejected -> Failed('...locked by another account') and, if the attempt was auto-reconnect, emit recoveryOffers. onDeviceConnected: PlaudDevice created with zeros, RecordingStore.addPairedDevice(sn, name) (also sets active), syncTime(), getConnectedDeviceVersion(), getChargingState()/getStorage() (battery/storage arrive via bleChargingState/bleStorage/blePowerChange), refreshRecordState(), checkFirmwareUpdate(), pending hotspot close if any, and fetchFileList after 3 s. Paired list is prefs-backed; getPairedDevices maps SN prefix to type (880 notepin, 881 notepro, 882 notepins, else note); Home lists other paired devices as rows that call switchDevice(sn) (disconnect, set active, 1.5 s, scan) and an '+ Add device' row that opens Scanning in add-device mode (which disconnects the current device first and waits 1.2 s before scanning).
nodes.notes: Cloud bind is fired on every bleBind status 0 (DeviceManager.kt:325-329). The app never persists the SN on tap, only after handshake success (DeviceConnectBottomSheet.kt:233-236).

nodes.behavior: Auto-reconnect: foreground-only. PlaudTemplateApp registers ActivityLifecycleCallbacks; on any background->foreground transition it waits 2 s and calls attemptReconnect() if lastConnectedDeviceSN and userId are set; MainActivity.onResume does the same. attemptReconnect(): no-op if suppressAutoReconnect, OTA in DOWNLOADING/INSTALLING/RESTARTING, no last SN, or state Connected/Connecting/Scanning; else resets the counter and startAutoReconnect(). Loop: while attempts < 10: startScan(); delay 30 s. Scan itself times out after 10 s (stopScan -> Disconnected). bleScanResult auto-connects (userInitiated=false) to lastConnectedDeviceSN when state is Scanning and not suppressed. Unexpected disconnect -> startAutoReconnect(initialDelay 2 s). Suppressed by: user disconnect, unpair, add-device scanning, OTA, Wi-Fi transfer, recovery; cleared on successful connect, explicit connect, switchDevice, end of OTA/Wi-Fi/add-device screen.
nodes.notes: No foreground service, no WorkManager, no AlarmManager: coroutine scopes are process-bound, so nothing runs once the process dies. README's '30-second interval timer, max 10 attempts' matches the code (CORROBORATED).

nodes.behavior: Unpair / disconnect / sign-out: disconnect() sets suppressAutoReconnect and calls PlaudDeviceAgent.disconnect() (device stays paired). unpair(): suppress, cloudUnbind(sn) fire-and-forget POST, RecordingStore.removePairedDevice (active falls back to first remaining), SyncManager.reset() (in-memory list only), state Disconnected, then PlaudDeviceAgent.depair(false) and disconnect on bleDepair callback or after 3 s. Unpair and Sign Out are refused while RecordingState.isActive ('would lose the recording in progress', PLA2-401). Sign Out == unpair current device; if no paired devices remain -> hasSkippedOnboarding=false and Welcome, else Activity.recreate(). DevicePanel shows name, SN, firmware (+Update), Disconnect, Unpair.
nodes.notes: Order 'cloud first, then local depair' is attributed to a 'lifecycle guide' that is not in the corpus.

nodes.behavior: Brick/lock recovery (app-owned orchestration): startDeviceRecovery(device): GET /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/binding?type&sn (Bearer) -> {is_bind (tri-state), bind_history[]}; fail if is_bind==true ('bound to another account'), or history empty, or BleDevice not cached. history = distinct().take(5). For each historical client_user_id: PlaudDeviceAgent.recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice, id); success only via bleBind status 0 within 25 s (bleConnectState 0/2 = fail), else disconnect, 1 s, next. On success: depair(false) and wait <=5 s for bleDepair, disconnect, 1.5 s, rescan for the same SN for <=20 s (depair changes the MAC), then connect() as the current user. Offered from DeviceConnectBottomSheet after a user-initiated connect fails, and from Home after an auto-reconnect handshake rejection.
nodes.notes: r7/r7-s12-k3-runtime-capture.md shows recoveryConnectBleDevice strips 'client_user_' and hyphens and writes the id into the k3 handshake with no network call (bytecode ALL.txt:2653-2761). Comments claim bind_history has one entry per device.bind event ('50+ duplicates') and is not client-scoped (DeviceManager.kt:1042-1043,1091-1093) - LINEAGE-grade cloud claims.

nodes.behavior: Cloud device binding as seen by the app: POST {host}/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind body {type, sn} with Authorization: Bearer <userAccessToken> after every successful handshake; HTTP 403 is interpreted as DEVICE_BOUND (another account) and surfaced as an alert 'already bound to another account. Unbind it from that account first'. POST .../sdk/unbind same body before local depair, result ignored. GET .../sdk/binding?type=&sn= returns is_bind + bind_history; a missing device is a bare 404 (comment). type is derived from the SN prefix on the phone. The host is RecordingStore.activeServerDomain (default platform-test.plaud.ai).
nodes.notes: The device accepted the BLE handshake before the cloud said 403: so the firmware lock and the cloud record can disagree; the app does nothing on 403 except alert (it stays connected). Baseline contradiction remains: SDK binary uses /api/devices/bind (inventory 128-136).

nodes.behavior: Account state: the User Access Token is a partner-issued JWT injected at build time from local.properties (PLAUD_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN -> BuildConfig.USER_ACCESS_TOKEN) or pasted at runtime (Settings -> Replace) into user_access_token_override; activeUserAccessToken = override ?: build value. userId = JWT payload 'sub' (base64url decode, no signature check), random UUID if the token is unparseable. Replace token: parse fails -> alert; same sub -> NiceBuildSdk.setPartnerToken(newToken) live ('renewal'); different sub -> RecordingStore.userId = user_id claim, prompt to exit ('Restart the app to switch accounts... a device bound to the previous account must be unpaired there'). X-Client-Id for transcription = JWT 'client_id' claim, fallback BuildConfig.PLAUD_CLIENT_ID; API key = api_key_override ?: BuildConfig.PLAUD_API_KEY, read per request. Server domain: Production platform-us.plaud.ai / Pre-release platform-us-pre.plaud.ai / Test platform-test.plaud.ai, DEFAULT Test, change requires restart; the Partner API base URL must be set manually because initSDK's customDomain is not forwarded (defaults to platform-jp per comment).
nodes.notes: Comment DeviceManager.kt:164-167: a US token sent to jp returns 401 CLIENT_USER_NOT_FOUND -> gen-key fails -> handshake fails (LINEAGE-grade cloud claim). There is no login/OAuth flow in the app; identity is entirely 'bring your own token'.

nodes.behavior: Settings screen contents (top to bottom): Automatic Sync toggle ('Auto transfer recordings via BLE when device is connected'); Device Firmware 'Version X' + Update button (visible when latestFirmwareVersion != null and != firmwareVersion; opens FirmwareUpdateSheet; refreshFirmwareCheck() on open); SDK Logs Export; User Access Token '<userId> · expires <date>' + Replace; API Key masked (8...4) + Replace; Server Environment '<label> · <domain>' + Switch; Version '<versionName> (<versionCode>)'; Sign Out ('This will disconnect and unpair your device').

Transcription flow (TranscriptionManager, IO scope, OkHttp 30 s connect / 120 s read+write): preconditions localPath exists, activeClientId and activeApiKey non-blank, extension != wav. Upload: file.readBytes() (whole file in memory), md5; POST {host}/developer/api/open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls {filesize, filetype} (Bearer token) -> FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize (default 5 MiB), Parts[{PresignedUrl, PartNumber}]; PUT each chunk to the presigned URL, collect ETag (quotes stripped); POST .../complete-upload {file_id, upload_id, part_list[{PartNumber, ETag}], filetype, file_md5} (Bearer) -> DownloadUrl. Submit: POST .../open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ {file_url, params:{transcribe:{language:'auto', model:'plaud-fast-whisper'}, vad:{decode_silence:false}, diarization:{enabled:false, return_embedding:false}}} headers X-Client-Id, X-Client-Api-Key -> transcription_id (or data.task_id). Poll: GET .../ai/transcriptions/{id} every 5 s, max 240 (20 min); status (or data.task_status) SUCCESS -> data.results array; FAILURE/REVOKED -> Failed; else Processing(status). A generation counter drops results from superseded tasks. Persisted: only RecordingStore.updateTranscript(id, resultsJson) on success; transcription_id, FileId, DownloadUrl are never stored. Empty results -> alert 'no speech was detected'. No summary request exists anywhere.
nodes.notes: Comments (LINEAGE-grade cloud claims): upload API rejects wav with FILE_TYPE_INVALID; 'the backend's opus pipeline currently returns empty results' (SyncManager.kt:788-790); server queue can back up (hence 20 min). Speaker labels are rendered from speaker_id 'SPEAKER_00' even though diarization is disabled (FileDetailActivity.kt:235-240). Result segment shape expected: {speaker_id, start (seconds), end, text, language} (TranscriptionManager.kt:30).

nodes.behavior: OTA: checkFirmwareUpdate runs on every connect and on Settings open. It is app-side because the SDK's own check needs an sdkToken from /api/oauth/sdk-token which '404s on platform-us' (comment). GET {host}/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/version/latest?type=<notepro|notepins|...>&sn=<sn>&current_version=-1 with header X-Device-Signature = PlaudDeviceAgent.getSnSignature() (re-signing via signAndStoreDeviceSn if empty). hasUpdate = version_code > deviceCode && download_url non-blank; response fields used: version_code, download_url, version_type (default 'V'), version_number, version_description, is_force, is_strong_guidance, file_md5. Version display: code = major*65536 + minor*256 + patch -> 'V1.0.10'; legacy 'V0147' passes through. Update button -> FirmwareUpdateSheet (380 dp, non-cancelable, starts OTA on first show, survives rotation) -> startFirmwareUpdate(): suppressAutoReconnect=true; downloadFirmware (progress 0-50%) -> installFirmware (50-100%, phases TRANSFERRING/TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING/DEVICE_RESTARTING) via facade; app watchdog = file.length/2 KB/s + 5 min; onInstallComplete -> COMPLETED (firmwareVersion updated locally, latest cleared) or FAILED; then suppress=false, 3 s, attemptReconnect(). Sheet: on COMPLETED waits <=60 s for Connected then 'Update complete!' and auto-dismiss after 2 s; on FAILED dismiss and alert; NO_UPDATE dismiss.
nodes.notes: is_force / is_strong_guidance are parsed but never enforced by the UI. Comment claims the facade has a hardcoded 5-minute install timeout and ~3-4 KB/s push speed (DeviceManager.kt:948-955) - unverified here.

nodes.behavior: AppLog writes every message to Logcat AND Timber; the SDK plants a Timber FileLoggingTree so app lines land in the SDK's on-disk logs. The app overrides the SDK's res/raw/logback.xml: RollingFileAppender, pattern '%d [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg', files ${LOG_DIR}/plaud_sdk_yyyy-MM-dd_HH_%i.log, 20 MB per file, 168 hourly files, totalSizeCap raised 100 MB -> 500 MB, root INFO. Settings -> SDK Logs Export calls NiceBuildSdk.exportLog(ctx) which produces an encrypted '.plaud' package in cacheDir, shares it via FileProvider as application/octet-stream, then NiceBuildSdk.cleanupLogs(ctx). BLE SDK log level is forced to INFO to suppress OTA per-packet DEBUG spam. Cloud request logs include the first 16 chars of the bearer token and 300 chars of response bodies.
nodes.evidence: T/common/AppLog.kt:6-31; RES/raw/logback.xml:2-33; T/ui/settings/SettingsFragment.kt:97-128; RES/xml/file_paths.xml:3; T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:183-187,1229,1237,1048-1054; build/evidence/javap/ALL.txt:7355,7375 (exportLog/cleanupLogs exist)
nodes.notes: The .plaud encryption scheme is SDK-owned and not visible in the app (UNKNOWN here). Gradle pulls logback-android 2.0.0, slf4j, timber as SDK transitive deps (GRADLE:81-92).

nodes.behavior: Notifications, background work and offline: there are no <service>, <receiver>, WorkManager, AlarmManager, NotificationManager or POST_NOTIFICATIONS usages; permissions are BLE, location, INTERNET, network/Wi-Fi state only. All work runs in singleton CoroutineScopes (Main or IO + SupervisorJob) that die with the process. Offline: BLE sync/recording need no network except the SDK's async gen-key at init (connect waits <=10 s for isPartnerDataReady then proceeds with a warning); cloud bind/unbind failures are logged only; transcription errors surface as an alert with the HTTP status and are not queued or retried; during Wi-Fi fast transfer the phone has no internet (comment), so the partner API is unreachable.

Timing/retry constants (ms unless noted): foreground reconnect delay 2000; auto-reconnect initial 2000, interval 30000, max 10 attempts; scan timeout 10000; switchDevice settle 1500; add-device disconnect settle 1200; RSA-ready wait 10000 (poll 200); post-connect file-list fetch 3000; record-stop -> sync 1000; record-state fallback 1500; record-start UI ack 4000; depair wait 3000 (unpair) / 5000 (recovery); recovery handshake 25000, rescan 20000, max 5 ids, inter-attempt 1000, post-depair 1500; Wi-Fi idle grace 1500, delete confirm 15000, device self-close 20000, post-transfer reconnect 1500; OTA watchdog fileLen/2KBps + 300000, post-OTA reconnect 3000, sheet reconnect wait 60000, dismiss 2000/800; transcription poll 5000 x 240, OkHttp 30 s/120 s/120 s, default chunk 5 MiB; banner fade 250, Completed banner hide 2000; waveform tick 100; recording timers 500/1000; player progress 200. CONNECT_TIMEOUT 30000 and HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT 60000 are declared but never referenced. No exponential backoff anywhere.

FileDetail screen: header name + 'MMM d, yyyy · HH:mm · Xm Ys' + Synced/Pending badge; Summary block only if summaryText non-blank (never); Transcript rendered as 'Speaker N · HH:MM:SS\n<text>' paragraphs parsed tolerantly from a bare array or {segments|transaction|list|data}, text from content|text|sentence, time from start_time/startTime (ms) or start (s); empty state: 'Generate recording insights' + button when synced, 'Sync this recording first' otherwise. Inline ExoPlayer (media3 1.3.1) with +/-5 s and slider, chosen because OEM MediaPlayer fails on Ogg/Opus; OpusRepair applied to .opus paths before play. More menu: Export Audio (re-exports from the DEVICE via PlaudDeviceAgent.exportAudio into cacheDir/export and shares via FileProvider - does not share the existing local file), Rename (local only), Copy Summary (hidden), Copy Transcript, Delete (local only, confirms 'permanently delete').
nodes.notes: The tolerant parser (device-cache shapes 'transaction', numeric 'speaker', start_time ms) hints at other transcript shapes Plaud handles elsewhere (LINEAGE-grade hint, source unknown).

nodes.behavior: Device facts the app encodes: SN prefixes 880 NotePin, 881 NotePro, 882 NotePin S, 888/other Note; firmware version code arithmetic major*65536+minor*256+patch with V/T prefix, install validation regex '^[VT]\d+$'; device drops BLE while in Wi-Fi AP mode and self-closes the hotspot after ~2 min; depair changes the advertised MAC; battery reported -1 until first bleChargingState; SDK 1.0.9 may report an empty BLE name; device answers openWiFi status 4 when busy; record-start ack takes ~1 s; a firmware locked by another account accepts GATT but rejects/drops the handshake (Android: connect-fail state 2 after ~10 s).
nodes.notes: These are claims embedded in comments; treat as high-quality hints, not proven device behaviour.

nodes.behavior: Cloud endpoints called directly by the app (not by the SDK), all under https://{activeServerDomain}/developer/api: GET /open/partner/sdk/version/latest (X-Device-Signature); GET /open/partner/sdk/binding, POST /open/partner/sdk/bind, POST /open/partner/sdk/unbind (Bearer userAccessToken); POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls, POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload (Bearer); POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/, GET /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/{id} (X-Client-Id + X-Client-Api-Key); plus PUT to S3 presigned URLs. Endpoints reached only through the SDK (gen-key, sn-sign, metadata, partner base URL) are per the frozen baseline. NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl(host) is called before initSDK to steer the SDK's partner API to the same host.
nodes.notes: No endpoint for listing recordings, summaries, memory, search, subscription or entitlement is referenced anywhere in the app: those product layers are absent from this template.

nodes.behavior: No subscription/entitlement/quota logic exists in the Android template: no paywall, no plan check, no usage counters; the only gating is 'Client ID or API key not configured' before transcription and HTTP errors afterwards.
nodes.evidence: T/managers/TranscriptionManager.kt:96-99; grep of T/** for 'subscription|entitle|quota|plan' yields nothing (all 40 files read)
nodes.notes: Billing is implied by the developer-portal API keys (baseline inventory 'still needs issued keys and bills').

nodes.text: Default server environment is Test (platform-test.plaud.ai) in a public template (T/storage/RecordingStore.kt:133-135, iOS parity ios RecordingStore.swift:131): unclear whether partners are expected to ship against prod, and what differs between prod/pre/test backends.

'Export Audio' re-exports the recording from the DEVICE via PlaudDeviceAgent.exportAudio instead of sharing the already-downloaded local file (T/managers/SyncManager.kt:595-612; T/ui/filedetail/FileDetailActivity.kt:469-495) even though the device copy was deleted after sync (746-764); what the SDK returns for a session no longer on the device, or when disconnected, is not visible in the app.

The README claims 'BLE sync with auto-download on connect' and the Settings copy says 'when device is connected', but the Android code only performs a silent list fetch on connect (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:491-500; T/managers/SyncManager.kt:101-104,650-654). Whether iOS or production apps behave differently is not established here.

handleFileList replaces the whole store each fetch, dropping unsynced rows for sessions absent from the device and re-stamping deviceSN with the active device; registerWifiFiles writes deviceSN='' (T/managers/SyncManager.kt:341-356,616-643). No explanation for the empty SN or for discarding rows.

Synced audio is kept in cacheDir/export (OS-evictable) while filesDir/audio/<sid>.opus and clearAll() are dead code (T/storage/RecordingStore.kt:224-244); whether this is an oversight or intentional, and what the SDK-chosen output file name is, is unknown.

android:allowBackup="true" (MANIFEST:23) with no rules: whether Google auto-backup restores prefs/recordings.json (leaving isSynced rows with missing audio) has not been observed; the code comment about the token 'expired after a reinstall' (WelcomeActivity.kt:52-53) hints prefs did not come back in Plaud's QA.

handlePcmData is never called and the facade has no blePcmData (T/managers/RecordingManager.kt:166-178; ALL.txt grep): how the Android 'live PCM waveform' is supposed to be fed is unexplained; the waveform is flat in this source.

bleDeleteFile status is ignored and a synced file whose device delete failed is never re-deleted (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:403-405; T/managers/SyncManager.kt:622-627): unclear how device storage is reclaimed in that case.

CONNECT_TIMEOUT (30 s) and HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (60 s) are declared but unused (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:50-51); the actual connect timeout is inside the SDK (comment: ~10 s connect-fail on Android, 296-300).

summaryText and 'Copy Summary' exist with no producer; the button copy says 'Transcribe and summarize' but only transcription is requested (T/ui/filedetail/FileDetailActivity.kt:130-131; T/managers/TranscriptionManager.kt:193-201). Which cloud API would produce a summary for partner apps is not in the corpus.

transcription_id is never persisted (T/managers/TranscriptionManager.kt:203-211): a task started before process death is unrecoverable from the app; whether the cloud retains results retrievable later is UNKNOWN (no list endpoint used).
checkFirmwareUpdate always sends current_version=-1 (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:555-556) and ignores is_force/is_strong_guidance; server semantics of -1 and of forced updates are unknown.
Firmware version code arithmetic (major*65536+minor*256+patch) vs legacy 'V0147' short codes (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:509-519): which device models use which scheme is not stated.

Comments cite documents absent from the corpus: 'sdk-requests-android-parity.md' #11/#13/#14, 'PARTNER_API_GUIDE.md', 'lifecycle guide §3.1/§3.2/§3.3/§4.5', tickets PLA2-309/312/317/321/323/325/330/331/401 (grep of reference/** finds none).

bind_history is described as not client-scoped (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:1042-1043): the cloud may return other partners' client_user_ids to any bearer of a token for that SN — privacy/authorisation model unexplained.

On POST sdk/bind returning 403 the app stays BLE-connected and merely alerts (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:1204-1213): the device accepted the handshake while the cloud says another account owns it; which layer is meant to enforce exclusivity is unclear.
userId falls back to a random UUID when the JWT is unparseable (T/ui/onboarding/WelcomeActivity.kt:77-91) and initSDK is still called with that token; resulting SDK/cloud behaviour is unknown.

Comment claims 'the backend's opus pipeline currently returns empty results' and 'upload API rejects wav (FILE_TYPE_INVALID)' (T/managers/SyncManager.kt:788-790; T/managers/TranscriptionManager.kt:100-105) while another comment says 'New syncs export OPUS' — the format history and current backend acceptance matrix are unexplained.

Wi-Fi join requires the user to 'tap Join when prompted' (RES/values/strings.xml:120): the network-request mechanism (WifiNetworkSpecifier vs legacy) and credential exchange live in the SDK and are not visible here.

The Android SDK facade's checkFirmwareUpdate reportedly requires /api/oauth/sdk-token which '404s on platform-us' (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:523-529), consistent with the baseline's unresolved /api vs /developer/api contradiction (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:128-136).

Recovery uses the current user's sn-sign/RSA material for a handshake with a historical id (comment T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:1111-1115): why the firmware accepts a signature from a different client than the id it checks is not explained.

README 'File Sync: BLE sync with auto-download on connect' vs Android code: connect only triggers a silent fetchFileList; downloads happen only after a recording stops with auto-sync on (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:491-500; T/managers/SyncManager.kt:101-104,650-654; T/managers/RecordingManager.kt:139-147).

README 'Recording: real-time recording with live PCM waveform' (and iOS blePcmData/JXRecordVolumer) vs Android: no PCM callback wired, waveform never fed (T/managers/RecordingManager.kt:166-178; ALL.txt has no blePcmData).
README 'Audio Playback: MP3 playback with floating player' vs Android: inline ExoPlayer inside FileDetail, no floating player (T/ui/filedetail/FileDetailActivity.kt:276-346).

iOS stores localPath as a file name relative to Documents (ios RecordingStore.swift:196-204) while Android stores an absolute path under cacheDir/export (T/managers/SyncManager.kt:418-420,749); Android pref keys are snake_case and lack a separate activeDeviceSN key (T/storage/RecordingStore.kt:13-18) vs iOS camelCase with activeDeviceSN (RecordingStore.swift:11-16).

Code comments disagree with each other on export format: 'New syncs export OPUS' (T/managers/TranscriptionManager.kt:100-101) vs AudioExportFormat.MP3 everywhere (T/managers/SyncManager.kt:398,791) and 'new syncs use MP3' in the user-facing error (TranscriptionManager.kt:104).

Baseline contradiction persists: SDK binary paths /api/devices/bind, /api/sdk/latest-version, /api/files/upload-s3/* vs this app's /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind, /sdk/version/latest, /files/upload/* (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:128-136); the app's own comment says the SDK's firmware check hits /api/oauth/sdk-token which 404s on platform-us (T/managers/DeviceManager.kt:523-529).
Settings subtitle 'Auto transfer recordings via BLE when device is connected' (RES/values/strings.xml:98) vs actual trigger (after recording stop only).

nodes.role: CLOUD_OBSERVED (community clients that talk to the live consumer web API api*.plaud.ai with the user's own account token) plus CORROBORATED where >=2 of the four clients agree independently. Nothing here is PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE or PROVEN_BYTECODE; every field/endpoint is what a companion observed or hypothesised, and each finding says which. No endpoint was called; no token was used; the browser-token extraction mechanisms are described from source only.

nodes.behavior: Regional routing: the API answers HTTP 200 with envelope {status:-302, msg:'user region mismatch', data:{domains:{api:'https://api-<region>.plaud.ai'}}} when an account is served from another region; clients re-issue the call against that host. Region keys observed in JWTs: aws:us-west-2 (api.plaud.ai), aws:eu-central-1 (api-euc1), aws:ap-southeast-1 (api-apse1). applaud notes accounts can be migrated between regions so the JWT region claim may be stale.

nodes.behavior: Response envelope convention: JSON {status:number, msg:string, request_id?} where status 0 = success; business errors ride on HTTP 200 with negative status (e.g. -302 region, -1 'session not authorized', -12 on transsumm). Clients must check body.status, not only HTTP status.

nodes.behavior: OTP login flow: POST /auth/otp-send-code {username:<email>} -> {status:0, token:<otp session token>} (may -302 redirect, riffado caps at 3 hops); POST /auth/otp-login {code, token} -> access_token (top-level or data.access_token). The returned token is a long-lived user token (UT); riffado documents ~300 days observed and that no refresh token is issued (migration 0012 added refresh_token, 0014 dropped it).
nodes.notes: Contradicted on lifetime by plaud-toolkit (see disagreements): password-login tokens are ~30 days.

nodes.behavior: Password login flow (plaud-toolkit): POST /auth/access-token, form-urlencoded username/password -> {status, access_token, token_type}. Every login mints a NEW session (JWT `sid`) and the backend evicts older sessions for the account, logging the phone app out; token lifetime is ~30 days (comment explicitly retracts an earlier ~300-day assumption).
nodes.notes: Included for cross-source comparison; session eviction on login is a product behaviour not visible in riffado/applaud.

nodes.behavior: web.plaud.ai browser storage (documented mechanism only, not executed): legacy accounts keep the long-lived user token in localStorage under key `tokenstr` (LevelDB key `_https://web.plaud.ai\x00\x01tokenstr`, value `bearer eyJ...`), riffado calls the same key `pld_tokenstr` and instructs `JSON.parse(localStorage.pld_tokenstr).replace(/^bearer /i,'')` (value is a JSON-encoded string). Other localStorage keys are prefixed `PLADU_<email>_...` and `PLADU_<uid>_bearer eyJ..._welcomeFileShown`. Newer accounts no longer expose tokenstr (applaud issue #31) and authenticate with HttpOnly cookies `pld_ut` and `pld_urt` on host plaud.ai (riffado connector changelog: 'Plaud authenticates with an HttpOnly session cookie no page JavaScript can read').

Described only; this harness never runs it. Note the key-name disagreement: applaud `tokenstr`, riffado `pld_tokenstr` -- likely the web app renamed the key; UNKNOWN which is current.

nodes.behavior: Cookie session model (applaud, ported from rovenotes-cloud): three tokens -- UT `pld_ut` (~1 day), URT `pld_urt` (~30 days, cookie Path=/auth/refresh-user-token in the test fixture), WT (workspace token, the bearer for data endpoints). Refresh: POST /auth/refresh-user-token with header `cookie: pld_ut=..; pld_urt=..`, body {} -> envelope status 0 and Set-Cookie of fresh pld_ut and (near expiry) rotated pld_urt. Plaud emits several Set-Cookie lines per response with Max-Age=0 clearers FIRST and the real value LAST; sometimes only one of the two cookies is set ('Plaud's behavior here is erratic'). JWT claims used: exp, iat, region, sid (or ut_sid).

nodes.behavior: Workspace token model: GET /team-app/workspaces/list?need_personal_workspace=true (Bearer UT) -> data.workspaces[] {workspace_id 'ws_...', member_id 'mem_...', name/workspace_name, role, status, workspace_type ('0' = personal), region?, api_domain?, created_at?, creator_user_id?}; POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{workspace_id} (Bearer UT, body {}) -> data {status, workspace_token, expires_in (86400 in fixtures), wt_expires_at, refresh_token, refresh_expires_in (2592000), refresh_expires_at, workspace_id, member_id, role}. WT JWT claims (from riffado's HAR-derived fixture): sub, aud:'', client_id:'web', region, jti, mfa_method:'skipped', mid:'mem_...', role:'admin', ut_ref:<sha256-like hex>, ver:1, wid:'ws_...', wtype:'0', iat, exp. UT JWT: sub, aud, client_id, region, iat, exp (no ut_ref/wid). Mint 401 = UT dead; other 4xx = stale workspace id (relist).

Real OAuth from a third-party origin is blocked by Google authorized-origins, so companions fall back to token paste or a browser extension that hands over the web session token.
nodes.notes: Product behaviour of Plaud's auth: identities are keyed by provider, not email.

nodes.behavior: Edge/WAF: api*.plaud.ai sits behind Cloudflare; non-browser User-Agents ('node', 'applaud/x.y.z', undici) get 403, sometimes an HTML challenge page on 200/403. riffado spoofs full Chrome headers (sec-ch-ua, origin https://web.plaud.ai, referer, sec-fetch-*) when proxying, routes through Webshare residential proxies, and needed a Chrome JA3/TLS fingerprint (wreq-js) because Cloudflare scores ASN and TLS fingerprint independently. plaud-api sends `app-platform: web` and `edit-from: web` headers and appends a random `r` query/body param.

nodes.behavior: riffado incremental sync semantics (companion-side, CLOUD_OBSERVED inputs): pages of 50 sorted edit_time desc, up to 20 pages, 5 concurrent downloads; identity key (userId, plaud_file_id) (migration 0019 relaxed the original global UNIQUE(plaud_file_id)); change key version_ms stored as plaud_version -- equal => skip, different => re-download and overwrite; user deletion is a tombstone (deleted_at) so re-sync never resurrects; stop rules: short page, 2 consecutive no-change pages (unless content import still has gaps), storage cap. HTTP 401 anywhere => plaud_connections.invalidated_at set and needsReconnect; a later successful sync clears it. Server worker ticks every 5 min for users not synced in 4 min (max 20/tick).

nodes.behavior: applaud incremental sync semantics: Phase 1 walks /file/simple/web (50/page, <=200 pages, is_trash=2 when importing Plaud-trashed items), upserts by id, renames the local folder if filename changed, updates is_trash/plaud_is_summary; Phase 2 fetches missing assets per row (metadata.json = full /file/detail, audio.ogg via temp-url, transcript via transsumm then content_list fallback, summary.md); Phase 3 probes Plaud-trashed rows for transcript/summary every 6h (25/scheduled, 100/manual). Local soft delete purges after 7 days and adds the id to sync_ignore so it is never re-imported. transcript_ready webhook fires only on the null->set transition.

nodes.text: POST /ai/transsumm/{id} returns status:-12 with empty data_result for recordings older than ~March 2026 while their transcript/summary remain available as content_list S3 artifacts (applaud poller.ts:337-340). Meaning of -12 and the cutoff are unknown.
data_result_summ is a JSON-encoded string for normal recordings but a structured object for very short recordings (applaud transcript.ts:33-35).
On EU/APAC regional servers, /file/simple/web called with a UT returns HTTP 200 and an empty list instead of 401/403 (riffado 66 test:6-11); on the global server a UT works. Enforcement rule unknown.
/device/list can return HTTP 200 {status:-1, msg:'session not authorized'} with no data_devices after a WT->UT fallback (riffado 231 test:7-13).

Cloud audio downloads are Ogg/Opus with OpusTags vendor 'PALUD.AI' yet labelled .mp3 / audio/mpeg, even when is_opus=0 is requested (riffado 160; baseline U19). What is_opus toggles and whether the cloud transcodes or only re-tags device audio is unknown.

/auth/refresh-user-token emits multiple Set-Cookie lines with Max-Age=0 clearers first, sometimes sets only pld_ut or only pld_urt ('erratic'), and pld_urt is path-scoped to /auth/refresh-user-token (applaud session.ts:91-113,389-395; session.test.ts:687).
Password login mints a new `sid` and evicts other sessions (logs the phone app out) while OTP/cookie sessions apparently coexist (toolkit auth.ts:5-13). Session-limit policy unknown.
OTP login for a Google/Apple-created account yields a separate empty account under the same email (riffado #65) -- identity keyed by provider; whether linking is possible is unknown.

Web app moved from localStorage `tokenstr` to HttpOnly cookies for newer accounts (applaud detect.ts:1-7; riffado CHANGELOG.md:27) yet riffado still documents `pld_tokenstr`; which accounts see which is unknown.
Token lifetimes vary by acquisition path (~300 d OTP UT per riffado, ~30 d password token per toolkit, ~1 d pld_ut per applaud); no source explains the policy.
Workspace-token mint returns refresh_token / refresh_expires_in (~30 d) that no client uses; what it refreshes is unknown (riffado types/plaud.ts:80-95).

plaud-api must PATCH trans_result/ai_content/outline_result/extra_data.task_id_info back onto the file after polling transsumm 'to persist' them (transcriptions.py:106-144), implying AI results are client-persisted; riffado/applaud see is_trans/is_summary and content_list populated without doing this (for app-created recordings). Which actor persists results is unknown.
Whether POST /ai/transsumm with an empty body (applaud) triggers new processing/billing or only reads cached results is unknown.

Content item types 'transaction_polish', 'outline', 'sum_multi_note', and detail fields embeddings, download_path_mapping, has_thought_partner, extra_data, plus transsumm fields ppc_status, auto_save, data_source_result, data_note_result, download_link_map, outline_task_status have no explained semantics (applaud detail.ts:5,26-30; transcript.ts:43-54).

List-row fields ori_ready, wait_pull, is_markmemo, edit_from, filetype, keywords, scene (101 for web uploads; device value unknown) are unexplained (riffado types/plaud.ts:14-38; applaud shared/recording.ts:1-24).

Summaries ship with unresolved template variables ($[audio_start_time], $[audio_end_time], '[Insert …]') and logo/image URLs that require Plaud cookies (applaud summarySanitize.ts:18-26); the templating layer is server-side and invisible.

Summary metadata summary_id format '20251119154839-v2@<hex>-1', state:10, category 'Chat Note', summ_type 'CASUAL-CONVERSATION' vs 'REASONING-NOTE' (riffado plaud-content.test.ts:24-31; plaud-api) -- the template/version scheme is unknown.

plaud-api adds a random `r` parameter to every request and headers app-platform:web / edit-from:web (session.py:43-46,86-99); whether the server requires them or uses edit-from for the row's edit_from attribution is unknown.
Accounts can apparently be migrated between regions so the JWT region claim goes stale and -302 corrects it (applaud routes/auth.ts:262-267); migration policy unknown.

riffado asserts api.plaud.cn is 'the same backend' as .ai because the OTP validation envelope is byte-identical (servers.ts:39-48) -- unverified and contradicts its own statement that .cn accounts do not exist on .ai.
/user/me data_state.membership_type is the only entitlement signal observed; its values and mapping to Plaud plans (Starter/Pro/Unlimited etc.) are unknown (toolkit client.ts:92).
Trash write path: PATCH /file/{id} {is_trash:true} vs POST /file/trash {file_ids} -- toolkit tries both; which is real is unknown.
Cloudflare scores egress ASN and TLS JA3 fingerprint independently (riffado CHANGELOG.md:112); exact WAF rules unknown.

`version` vs `version_ms` vs detail `file_version` vs transsumm `file_version`: which bump on which edits (rename, trash, transcript edit, speaker rename) is unknown; riffado assumes version_ms changes on any update.

User-token lifetime: riffado says OTP UT ~300 days (203 test:6-7, docs:73-79, schema.ts:211); plaud-toolkit says password-login tokens are ~30 days and explicitly retracts a 300-day assumption (core/src/auth.ts:5-13); applaud's cookie pld_ut is ~1 day with a ~30-day pld_urt (session.ts:7-11). Likely three different token classes/generations; UNRESOLVED which applies to a given account.

Refresh tokens: riffado docs state 'Plaud's API does not issue refresh tokens' (connect-plaud-account.mdx:75) and dropped its refresh_token column (migration 0014), yet the WT mint response riffado types includes refresh_token/refresh_expires_in (types/plaud.ts:80-95) and applaud refreshes via /auth/refresh-user-token (session.ts:369-396). Refresh exists for cookie sessions and WTs; not for OTP UTs.

Is a WT required? riffado #66: regional (EU/APAC) /file/simple/web silently returns an empty list with a UT; plaud-api and plaud-toolkit call /file/simple/web with a single token and no WT at all (recordings.py:46-56, core/client.ts:59-63); applaud legacy mode uses the raw tokenstr JWT directly (routes/auth.ts:35-77). Whether WT enforcement is regional-only, account-generation-only, or time-dependent is UNKNOWN.

/user/me response shape: riffado reads email at body.email or body.data.email (auth.ts:185-195); applaud (with WT) and plaud-toolkit read body.data_user.email plus data_state.membership_type (first-party.ts:73-74; client.ts:84-94). riffado's fixtures are synthetic.

Transcript delivery path: riffado imports segments from content_list 'transaction' data_link and marks the body shape UNVERIFIED (content.ts:12-15); applaud's primary path is POST /ai/transsumm/{id} data_result with fields start_time/end_time/content/speaker/original_speaker (transcript.ts:6-12), content_list only for pre-March-2026 rows returning status -12 (poller.ts:337-340); plaud-api reads trans_result from POST /file/list rows (transcriptions.py:150-161). Three paths, one entity; consistency not verified.

transsumm request body: applaud posts {} (transcript.ts:57-62); plaud-api posts {is_reload, summ_type:'REASONING-NOTE', summ_type_type:'system', info, support_mul_summ:true} (transcriptions.py:54-70). Unknown whether the body affects processing or billing.

temp-url response shape: riffado's own unit test mocks {code:0,msg,data:{temp_url,temp_url_opus}} (plaud.test.ts:188-195) while its production type is top-level {status,temp_url,temp_url_opus} (types/plaud.ts:47-51); applaud/plaud-api use top-level temp_url. riffado's test mock is not evidence.

Bearer scheme casing: plaud-api sends 'bearer <jwt>' lowercase (session.py:60) and localStorage stores 'bearer eyJ' (applaud leveldb.ts:81-82); riffado/applaud/toolkit send 'Bearer'. Both evidently accepted.
localStorage key name: applaud 'tokenstr' (leveldb.ts:14) vs riffado 'pld_tokenstr' (plaud-connect-tabs.tsx:42-49); applaud also says newer accounts no longer expose tokenstr at all (detect.ts:1-7).

Region key derivation: applaud maps hostnames to 'aws:us-west-2|eu-central-1|ap-southeast-1' (client.ts:4-8); toolkit collapses to 'us'|'eu' by substring 'euc1'/'eu-' (client.ts:52; auth.ts:73-74); plaud-api knows only default+apse1 (_endpoints.py:7-10); baseline lists api-usw1 which riffado treats as unknown/custom.
Trash mechanism: toolkit tries PATCH /file/{id} {is_trash:true} then POST /file/trash {file_ids} (obsidian PlaudClient.ts:88-125); no other client writes trash; which endpoint is real is UNKNOWN.

Extra request headers: plaud-api sends app-platform:web, edit-from:web and a random 'r' param (session.py:43-46,86-99); riffado/applaud omit them and report success -- either optional or affecting server-side 'edit_from' attribution only.

nodes.behavior: The user token is a JWT whose payload carries sub, user_id (falls back to sub), exp and client_id; the template derives X-Client-Id from the JWT client_id claim so it 'always matches the account/environment', with Info.plist/BuildConfig as fallback. Signature is never verified client-side.
nodes.notes: Confirms CLIENT_ID is embedded in every user token; API_KEY is not.

nodes.behavior: Handshake (bind) token derivation is local: the SDK parses the initSDK JWT, regex-extracts the `sub` claim, strips a leading 'client_user_' prefix, deletes '-' characters, and uses the result as the BLE handshake token; if parsing fails it falls back to the explicit bindToken/deviceToken argument. An empty result makes the pen handshake abort with the SDK's UUID_IS_EMPTY code.
nodes.evidence: build/evidence/jadx-out/sources/sdk/NiceBuildSdk.java:140-175 (resolveHandshakeToken); reference/plaud-org/embedded-capacitor/android/app/src/main/java/ai/plaud/pwademo/PlaudSdkPlugin.java:414-425,826-832 (parseUserIdFromJWT); plaud-sdk-public/README.md:328 ('Handshake token is auto-parsed from the sub field'); docs/protocol-ledger.md:1423-1451 (frozen: same transform, RUNTIME_PROVEN)
nodes.notes: So 'client_user_<uuid>' is the cloud's subject-id format for partner users; the device stores the 32-char hyphen-less form. The wrappers' `userId`/`deviceToken` argument is therefore only a fallback, contrary to the wrapper comments that say it 'binds the device to the user' (PlaudSdkModule.swift:112-113).

nodes.behavior: Developer Portal issues three credentials per application: CLIENT_ID + CLIENT_SECRET (used only server-side for the partner token) and API_KEY (created under App Settings > API Keys; used with X-Client-Id for the Transcription API; explicitly NOT the client_secret). Portal URLs given as https://portal.plaud.ai and https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/portal.

File Upload API is a 3-step S3 multipart: (1) POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls, Bearer user token, {filesize, filetype} → {FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize, Parts[{PartNumber, PresignedUrl}]}; (2) PUT raw bytes of each ChunkSize slice to PresignedUrl with no auth, keep the ETag header (strip quotes); (3) POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload, Bearer user token, {file_id, upload_id, part_list[{PartNumber, ETag}], filetype, file_md5?} → {FileId, FileType, DownloadUrl, FileMd5?}. Demo backends restrict filetype to 'mp3' | 'opus'; template uses 5 MB chunks ('required by API').
nodes.notes: Capacitor must PUT from native (putBinary) because the remote-origin WebView blocks CORS and cannot read ETag (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:237-267; nextjs-demo/README.md:306-313). Content-Type is deliberately not set on the PUT to avoid S3 SignatureDoesNotMatch (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:248-251).

nodes.behavior: DownloadUrl returned by complete-upload is claimed valid for 24 hours and is what must be passed as file_url to the Transcription API. The Transcription API needs a public download URL; the File Upload API is optional if the partner already has one.

Transcription API: POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ with headers X-Client-Id + X-Client-Api-Key, body {file_url, params?}; GET /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/{transcription_id} same headers. Response {transcription_id, status, data}. Statuses: PENDING, RECEIVED, STARTED, PROGRESS (in flight), SUCCESS (data populated), FAILURE, REVOKED (terminal). data = {text, language, duration (s), results[{start, end, text, speaker_id?, language, language_probability}]}.
nodes.notes: Pipeline description ('language detection, noise reduction, ASR, Speech-to-text') is marketing/doc-claim (SKILL.md:10-11). Async job; no webhook is mentioned anywhere — polling only.

nodes.behavior: Transcription params object: transcribe.language (default 'auto', BCP-47), transcribe.detection_level ('segment'|'chapter', default segment), transcribe.model ('plaud-fast-whisper' | 'plaud-omni-3' | 'azure-fast-transcribe' — present in the TS type and every demo default, absent from the skill's param table), vad.decode_silence (false), diarization.enabled (false), diarization.return_embedding (false). All demos default to model 'plaud-fast-whisper', language auto, diarization off.
nodes.notes: Model names are the only enumeration of Plaud ASR models in the corpus. What 'plaud-omni-3' or 'azure-fast-transcribe' map to server-side is UNKNOWN.

nodes.behavior: Doc-claimed limits: file_url formats M4A, MP3, WAV; recordings exceeding 5 hours should be chunked. Device-side files are also claimed capped at 5 h per recording.
nodes.notes: Mismatch: the upload API demos accept filetype 'opus' (not in the M4A/MP3/WAV list) and never 'm4a'/'wav'.

nodes.behavior: Polling cadence differs by demo and is not a platform rule: template 5 s × 240 (20 min, 'server queue can back up'); Capacitor 5 s × 120 (~10 min); RN and Flutter 3 s for 3 min. RN/Flutter defensively parse alternate response shapes: id from `transcription_id` OR `data.task_id`; status from `status` OR `data.task_status`; text from `text`/`full_text`/`transcript`/`transcription`, `results[].text` or `segments[].text`, and a nested `data.data`.

nodes.notes: The defensive parsing is the strongest hint in the corpus that Plaud engineers observed more than one response shape from the live API; the alternate shape is otherwise undocumented.

nodes.behavior: Supported devices: Plaud Note Pro (SN prefix 881, type 'notepro') and NotePin S (882, 'notepins'); Plaud Note and original NotePin are explicitly NOT supported. The SDK's resolveDeviceType maps only 881/882 and logs 'unsupported SN prefix … defaulting to notepro' for anything else. The device type string + SN is the cloud registry key and must stay consistent across every API call.
nodes.notes: Wrappers and templates disagree on other prefixes: Android template/RN/Flutter/Capacitor map 880→'notepin', 888→'note' (DeviceManager.kt:791-797; PlaudSdkModule.kt:445-450; PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:391-396; PlaudSdkPlugin.java:853-857); iOS template maps 883→'notepin' (PlaudDevice.swift:68-76); the Flutter Android bridge infers supportWiFi from projectCode==881 (PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:524-526).

nodes.behavior: Device constraint (doc-claim, corroborated by code paths): a Plaud device can be bound to one application at a time; users must unbind before uninstalling or the device cannot be bound to another app (or the Plaud app) 'until it is recovered'. The firmware retains the previous user's client_user_id and rejects other handshakes (GATT connect succeeds, handshake is refused, link drops); the Android transport reports TOKEN_NOT_MARCH which the Capacitor demo renders as 'bound to a different user'.

Recovery flow ('brick recovery', lifecycle guide §3.3): GET /open/partner/sdk/binding?type&sn (Bearer user token) returns three-state is_bind (true/false/null='signed but never bound') and newest-first bind_history[] of client_user_ids; if is_bind==true the other owner must unbind; else dedupe bind_history, try up to N historical ids via PlaudDeviceAgent.recoveryConnectBleDevice(device, historicalUserId) (SDK ≥1.0.13; pins the historical id as handshake token and connects with isForceClear / PRE_HANDSHAKE_AND_CLEAR 0xFE20; reuses the current user's sn-sign/RSA material), on success depair, rescan (depair changes the device MAC), reconnect as current user. bind_history is NOT client-scoped and a missing device is a bare 404.

nodes.behavior: Cloud device binding is done at the APP layer in the template: POST /open/partner/sdk/bind after every successful connect (idempotent for same owner; 403 DEVICE_BOUND if bound to another account) and POST /open/partner/sdk/unbind before local depair ('cloud first, then local depair'); body {type, sn}, Bearer user token. iOS template says the SDK auto-reports metadata (reportDeviceMetadata) instead.

nodes.notes: Refines frozen ledger §4.4 ('cloud bind is never called by the SDK'): true for the SDK, but the PRODUCT does cloud-bind via the app. The wrappers (RN/Flutter/Capacitor) never call bind/unbind/binding — they only depair locally.

nodes.behavior: Android handshake prerequisites the integrator must perform (iOS does them internally): (1) NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl('https://'+customDomain) BEFORE initSDK because the SDK's PartnerRetrofitClient hardcodes https://platform-jp.plaud.ai and ignores customDomain — otherwise a US token gets 401 CLIENT_USER_NOT_FOUND on gen-key and every handshake fails; (2) poll NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() (RSA key pair fetched asynchronously by initSDK; 10 s cap); (3) NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn) (suspend) or signDeviceSnAsync from Java.

nodes.behavior: iOS partner-API facade (unobfuscated): PlaudPartnerApiManager.shared.setUserAccessToken/getUserAccessToken, signDeviceSn(deviceType:sn:) → PlaudPartnerSnSignResponse{signature}, generateRsaKeyPair() → PlaudPartnerGenKeyResponse{publicKey, privateKey}; errors noUserAccessToken / unauthorized(detail) / serverError(code, body). nodes.behavior: SDK initialisation contract: initSDK(userAccessToken, customDomain) where customDomain is the bare host (e.g. platform-us.plaud.ai; the SDK prefixes https://). iOS also exposes a legacy initSDK(hostName, appKey, appSecret, bindToken, …, customDomain, partnerToken) and getTestAppKey/getTestAppSecret; token rotation via setUserAccessToken(newToken). Android initSDK(context, userAccessToken, customDomain[, extra Map]).

nodes.behavior: Export pipeline: exportAudio decodes an on-device recording to a local file in a private per-app dir (iOS Documents/PlaudExports, Android filesDir/PlaudExports) in pcm(0)/mp3(1)/wav(2)/opus(3); MP3 recommended because it plays everywhere and is accepted by the upload API. Template flow on connect: getFileList → exportAudio(.mp3) → deleteFile on device ('files belong to the phone after sync; device files are always unsynced'). The high-level facade handles E2EE decrypt, cache and transcode (Android: 'download, cache, E2EE decrypt, transcode').

nodes.behavior: Android BleFile carries only sessionId/fileSize/attribute/scene, so wrappers fill sn/channels/isOgg from the connected BleDevice and derive duration via BleFile.calculateOpusDuration(fileSize, channels)/1000 (80 bytes per 20 ms frame per channel; Ogg-container files read slightly long). iOS BleFile has sn/channels/isOgg/duration(). Consequence: connect before getFileList on Android.

Template app local behaviour: launch routing on paired devices + userId; auto-reconnect scan 2 s after foreground, 30 s interval timer, max 10 attempts; multi-device via RecordingStore.pairedDeviceSNs/activeDeviceSN with one BLE connection at a time; live PCM waveform from blePcmData (640-byte frames, 16 kHz mono) at 100 ms UI timer; Settings screen can replace user token and API key at runtime (UserDefaults overrides) and switch server domain (restart to apply).

Wi-Fi fast transfer (claimed ~10x BLE): app calls setDeviceWiFi(open:true) → bleWiFiOpen(status, wifiName, wholeName, wifiPass) → PlaudWiFiAgent.shared.connectWifi(ssid, password, 60) → wifiHandshake(status 0) → exportAudioViaWiFi / startDownloadAll (wifiDownloadAllProgress/Completed); iOS needs the Hotspot Configuration + wifi-info entitlements and NSLocalNetwork/NSLocation usage strings. Android: PlaudDeviceAgent.startWifiTransfer(userId, WifiTransferCallback with 12 required members: onConnectionStateChanged/onFileListReceived/onBatchDownload*/onFileDeleteCompleted/onError…). Low-level PlaudWiFiSDK.WiFiAgent runs listenPort(ssid), connectWifi(ssid, passphrase, 60, needRetry), a local WebSocket server, rate test, device logs, and Wi-Fi OTA push (startPushOTA, sendFilePackToPen).

nodes.behavior: Firmware OTA: iOS one-call flow checkFirmwareUpdate → PlaudFirmwareCheckResult{hasUpdate, currentVersion, latestVersion, versionCode, releaseNotes, downloadUrl, md5, isForce}; startFirmwareUpdate(progress:(phase .downloading/.installing/.restarting/.complete, pct), completion PlaudFirmwareUpdateResult{success, version, errorMessage}); pushFirmwareFile(filePath, toVersion). Android three-step checkFirmwareUpdate/downloadFirmware(MD5 verify)/installFirmware(BLE push + restart), FirmwareUpdateCallback. Template shows a bottom sheet, blocks auto-reconnect during OTA, waits for restart+reconnect. LatestVersionResponse fields: type, model, version_type, version_code, version_number, version_description, is_force, is_strong_guidance, file_md5, download_url.

Android firmware version check is done APP-side: GET /open/partner/sdk/version/latest?type&sn&current_version=-1 with header X-Device-Signature = the sn-sign signature (PlaudDeviceAgent.getSnSignature()), because the Android SDK's own checkFirmwareUpdate requires an internal sdkToken from appKey/appSecret via /api/oauth/sdk-token, 'an endpoint that does not exist on the developer platform (404 on platform-us)'. Response fields used: version_code, download_url; install validation requires version '^[VT]\d+$' (e.g. V66055).
nodes.notes: DISAGREES with r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:122-127 which lists version/latest under 'Bearer user_access_token', and adds a live-cloud claim (404) to r7's /api/oauth/sdk-token entry (lines 34-44).

nodes.behavior: Firmware-facing behaviours surfaced by the app layer: depair changes the device's advertised MAC (cached BleDevice becomes stale; must rescan); firmware retains the previous binder's client_user_id; a stale OS-level BONDED entry makes Android GATT service discovery hang and surfaces only as TIME_OUT after 10 s; device firmware versions look like 'V66055'; the device closes its Wi-Fi hotspot on a ~2 min firmware timeout if the app cannot send close over BLE.

Demo backend (Next.js, embedded-capacitor/nextjs-demo) owns five routes: POST /api/user-token {user_id} → {access_token, expires_in} (needs PLAUD_CLIENT_ID + PLAUD_SECRET_KEY; Node runtime); POST /api/transcription/presign {access_token, filesize, filetype} (proxies presign with the CLIENT-supplied user token); POST /api/transcription/complete {access_token, file_id, upload_id, part_list, filetype, file_md5?}; POST /api/transcription/submit {file_url, params?} (adds X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key from env); GET /api/transcription/status/[id]. Upstream failures map to 502, missing env to 500. Bytes never transit the backend — parts PUT natively to S3.

nodes.behavior: Why a native shell exists: iOS WebKit has no Web Bluetooth; on Android Web Bluetooth exists but the device conversation needs Plaud's proprietary pairing handshake, encrypted transport and AVC/OGG-Opus decode which live only in the native SDK. Capacitor 8 does not auto-register local plugins (manual registerPluginInstance in capacitorDidLoad / registerPlugin before super.onCreate).

No subscription, entitlement, quota or billing logic appears in any official Embedded source. The only gating is credential-based (partner token, user token, API key) and HTTP status handling (401 CLIENT_USER_NOT_FOUND, 403 DEVICE_BOUND, bare 404 for unknown device).

nodes.behavior: Platform/tooling constraints: iOS frameworks are arm64 device-only (no simulator slice); plaud-sdk-public says iOS 14.0+/Xcode 16/Swift 6.0.3 build, but Capacitor Package.swift declares .iOS(.v15) and RN/Flutter podspecs 15.1 ('the Plaud frameworks require it'); PlaudDeviceBasicSDK is a static framework whose localization bundle must be copied; Android minSdk 21 (AAR) / 24 (Flutter host), AAR has no POM so ~12 transitive deps are hand-declared (Retrofit, OkHttp, Gson, Guava, BouncyCastle, Conscrypt, Java-WebSocket, Timber, slf4j, logback-android, coroutines); Android emulator has no BLE. Template versionCode 42 / 1.0.42; Flutter port dated 2026-07-24.

Android runtime permission sets differ per wrapper: RN requests BLUETOOTH_SCAN+CONNECT+FINE+COARSE_LOCATION on API 31+ (BLUETOOTH/ADMIN+locations below); Flutter requests only SCAN+CONNECT on 31+ (FINE_LOCATION below); Capacitor SCAN+CONNECT on 31+ else FINE_LOCATION; the SDK's own sdk.permission.PermissionManager requests the full RN-style set. Bluetooth-off gate polls ~18 s (60 × 300 ms) then emits scanTimeout{reason:'bluetoothNotPoweredOn'}; permission refusal → 'permissionDenied' (Flutter/Capacitor event) or ERR_PLAUD_PERMISSIONS rejection (RN).

SDK obfuscation boundary: real public API is sdk.PlaudDeviceAgent, sdk.PlaudDeviceAgentListener, BleDevice/BleFile (and com.tinnotech.penblesdk.*); everything else in the AAR is obfuscated and changes between releases; there is no published Android SDK doc — the AAR bytecode and proguard.txt are the reference. iOS: verify against the .swiftinterface files because the generated ios-sdk-reference.md drifts.
nodes.notes: Justifies treating the .swiftinterface as the authoritative iOS facade map.

nodes.text: bind_history contains one entry per device.bind event with 50+ duplicates of the same client_user_id ('live-verified' per DeviceManager.kt:1083-1086) and is not client-scoped — no source explains why the cloud does not dedupe or scope it.
is_bind == null means 'signed but never bound' (PlaudAPIService.swift:244) — what 'signed' means server-side (sn-sign creating a registry row?) is not documented.
depair changes the device's advertised MAC address (DeviceManager.kt:429-431; DeviceManager.swift:113-116) — firmware rationale unknown.
SDK resolveDeviceType defaults unknown SN prefixes to 'notepro' with only a log warning (javap:1624-1666) — effect on sn-sign/bind for 880/883/888 devices unknown.

Android SDK's PartnerRetrofitClient hardcodes platform-jp while iOS PlaudDomainManager supports cn/us/jp with language auto-association — why the Android default is jp and whether cn is reachable for partners is unexplained.

nodes.behavior: Cloud binding is app-owned, not SDK-owned: after every bleBind(0) the template POSTs {type,sn} to /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind (Bearer userAccessToken; same-owner rebind idempotent; HTTP 403 DEVICE_BOUND surfaced as 'already bound to another account'). Unpair does cloud /sdk/unbind FIRST (best effort, idempotent) then local depair. GET /sdk/binding?type&sn returns three-state is_bind (true/false/null=signed-never-bound) and newest-first bind_history of client_user_ids (one entry per bind event, duplicates; not client-scoped; missing device = bare 404).

nodes.behavior: Brick recovery: query bind_history -> dedupe, take newest 5 -> for each id call PlaudDeviceAgent.recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice, historicalUserId) (SDK 1.0.13: pins the historical id as handshake token, connects with isForceClear = PRE_HANDSHAKE_AND_CLEAR 0xFE20 so firmware wipes stale key material, reuses the CURRENT user's sn-sign/RSA material, auto-restores identity after the attempt; 25 s per attempt) -> on bleBind(0) send depair (5 s wait for DepairRsp) -> disconnect -> rescan up to 20 s because 'depair changes the device MAC' -> reconnect as current user. GATT connect during recovery is NOT proof; depair sent before handshake completes is ignored by the device.

nodes.behavior: BLE push (OtaPushHelper = com.plaud.sdk.proto.p4): FotaInfo request opcode 50 = i(uid:long, fromVersion:String, toVersion:String, thirdVersion:int, fileSize:long, crc:int[, isSilent:boolean]) (iOS BleAgent.pushFotaInfo mirrors it; crc = CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE tntGetFileCrc, ledger §5.8/U13); device answers AppFotaPushRsp{uid…} (opcode 50) and then per-pack AppFotaPackRsp{uid…} (opcode 52) which the helper matches on 'portType'/'uid miss match'; data is read from a RandomAccessFile in chunks of 80 bytes (160 in an alternate mode p4.p()) with pacing constant d() = 40 or 160 depending on flag A, on a 'tnt-ble-fota-push-loops-pool' executor (Wi-Fi variant 'tnt-wifi-ota-push-pool', WifiOTAPackage msg 20/21/22); finish = f(uid,status) opcode 51 -> AppFotaPackFinishRsp; status=2 = 'waiting call message' (device asks for more), status=13 = 'Silent OTA transfer success, stopping transmission'. Error enum s0$i (20 values): RESTART(1), SEND_BLE_FAIL(2), SEND_BLE_COMMAND_FAIL(14), FILE_NOT_EXISTS(3), FILE_ERROR(4), USER_INTERRUPT(5), DEVICE_UPGRADE_FAIL(6), DEVICE_VERSION_NOT_MATCH(7), DEVICE_FLASH_WRITE_FAIL(8), OTA_FILE_SIZE_TOO_LARGE(11), DEVICE_WRITE_MORE_COUNT(9), DEVICE_U_DISK_MODE(10), BT_DISCONNECT(12), DEVICE_RECORDING(13), DEVICE_SPACE_LOW(15), WORKING_NOW(17), G101_NO_CHARGING(18), G101_POWER_LOW(19), G101_MODE_TRANS(20), DEVICE_MODE_NOT_MATCH(16). Template notes the helper logs ~5 lines per 80-byte packet (~200 lines/s) and real speed ~3-4 KB/s.

nodes.behavior: Install phases and restart/reconnect: Android FirmwareTransferPhase = TRANSFERRING, TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING, DEVICE_RESTARTING, UPGRADE_COMPLETE, TRANSFER_FAILED, UPGRADE_FAILED; internal detail strings add RECONNECTING_DEVICE, WAITING_UPGRADE_RESULT, UPGRADE_COMPLETE_SUCCESS/FAILED, REQUEST_RECONNECT; the facade reconnects the device itself ('【阶段3-重连】开始重连设备') and waits for the device's upgrade verdict (STICK_FOTA_RESULT_IND / deviceFotaResult), with a hard 300 000 ms (5 min) install timeout, a 'slow transfer' warning below 5.0 KB/s, and a device 'protection mechanism' message (status=5 / too many attempts: wait 10-15 min). iOS PlaudFirmwarePhase = downloading(0)/installing(1)/restarting(2)/complete(3) via startFirmwareUpdate(progress:completion:) or pushFirmwareFile(filePath:toVersion:). Templates suppress auto-reconnect during OTA, keep the sheet up until the device actually reconnects (60 s cap), and iOS notes 'SDK completion fires before device actually disconnects'. Pre-conditions enforced client-side: device connected, not already isFotaPushing; UI note: keep device charging, app open, device close.

nodes.behavior: Fast-transfer session (both platforms): app stops any BLE export, waits 1.5 s for device idle (device refuses openWiFi with status 4 'busy' / connect 1003), suppresses BLE auto-reconnect, then PlaudDeviceAgent.setDeviceWiFi(true) (BLE opcode 10 OpenWiFi, ledger §7) -> bleWiFiOpen(status, wifiName, wholeName, wifiPass) (SDK 1.0.9+ guarantees a non-empty pass by falling back to the SN-derived default; WifiAgentImpl.calculateWifiName='Plaud'+…, calculateWifiPassword) -> iOS waits 3 s then PlaudWiFiAgent.connectWifi(ssid, pass, 180) with internal NEHotspotConfiguration retry (needs Hotspot Configuration entitlement + location permission); Android WifiConnectionManager uses WifiNetworkSpecifier with a 30 000 ms wait -> phone-side WebSocket server on port 8081 -> HandshakeRequest{token,stamp} using the SAME BLE handshake token (WifiAgentImpl.startWifiTransfer calls NiceBuildSdk.resolveHandshakeToken; its String parameter, named 'userId' internally and 'sn' at the facade, does not seed the token) -> wifiHandshake(0) / onHandshakeCompleted -> app must explicitly getFileList (uid = now) or the device 'just heartbeats and closes'. Connection states: NONE, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, HANDSHAKING, READY, DISCONNECTED, ERROR (Android) / wifiIdle…wifiReady/wifiConnectFailed/wifiClosed with reasons personalHotspot/connectSlow/timeout/failed (iOS). BLE drops while the device is in AP mode.

nodes.behavior: Wi-Fi payload crypto scope: WifiAgentImpl.saveEncryptionKeys copies the BLE session's ChaCha20 key/nonce/AD and send/recv sequence before the transfer and picks 'AES-GCM' when wifiUseAes (capability bit 3) else 'ChaCha20-Poly1305'; encryptWifiMessage/decryptWifiMessage log seq and algo; missing keys -> 'Local ChaCha20 keys not available'. iOS SecretUtil exposes decryptWithFallback(preferAes:). Android IWifiTransferAgent.WifiTransferCallback has exactly 12 members: onConnectionStateChanged, onHandshakeCompleted, onFileListReceived, onTransferProgress, onFileTransferCompleted, onBatchDownloadStarted, onBatchDownloadProgress, onBatchDownloadCompleted, onFileDeleteCompleted, onWifiTransferStopped, onDeviceBatteryUpdate, onError. Raw downloadAllFiles writes the device stream verbatim to a 'PlaudOpus' directory (no E2EE decrypt/container), so templates drive exportAudioViaWiFi per file instead.

nodes.behavior: Wi-Fi teardown is device-led: after all exports the app issues ONE deferred batch delete (Android getWifiAgent().deleteFiles(list), 15 s confirm timeout; iOS PlaudWiFiAgent.deleteFile(sid,1) per id, 4 s) because deleting mid-session disrupts the WebSocket; then it waits (20 s cap) for the device to self-close after '3 heartbeats' (wifiClose 1000 = clean, also used when nothing to transfer); force-closing preempts the graceful exit and drops the device into a '~2.5 min fallback'. NiceBuildSdk.stopWifiTransfer / endWiFiTransfer also sends closeWiFi over BLE (opcode 13) when BLE is up; if BLE is down the device stays in Wi-Fi mode (blue LED) until its own ~2 min firmware timeout, so templates defer setDeviceWiFi(false) to the next BLE reconnect. A second openWiFi during connect is rejected with status 4 and orphans the first session.

nodes.behavior: BLE sync model: files belong to the phone after sync and device files are always unsynced. On connect (3 s delay, skipped while recording) getFileList -> for each session exportAudio(format MP3, channels 1) -> on completion deleteFile(sessionId) on the device (opcode 30, ledger §5.10). MP3 chosen because the partner transcription backend returns empty results for opus and rejects wav (FILE_TYPE_INVALID); iOS user export uses .wav. User-facing delete is local-only. Local store: recordings.json + SharedPreferences/UserDefaults keys last_connected_device_sn, paired_device_sns, paired_device_names, user_id, is_auto_sync_enabled (default true), fast_transfer_never_show; audio at files/audio/{sessionId}.opus, exports in cache/export. RecordingFile{id,sessionId,deviceSN,name,duration,createdAt=sessionId*1000,syncedAt,localPath,summaryText,transcriptJSON}; sessionId is a unix-seconds timestamp. Android BleFile exposes only sessionId/fileSize/attribute/scene/isMusic (no public duration; template reads Ogg granule position instead); iOS BleFile has sn,size,offset,timezone,zoneMin,scenes,penCollect,channels,nsAgc,isOgg,isMusic,duration().

Bluetooth-off is failed fast. Account switch (different JWT sub) requires app restart and 'a device bound to the previous account must be unpaired there before the new account can bind it'; same-sub token renewal applies live via setUserAccessToken/NiceBuildSdk.setPartnerToken (SDK refreshes RSA keys).

nodes.behavior: How Plaud launches GoReplay: a parameterised Jenkins pipeline builds the image and runs a long-lived container on the host network with NET_RAW/NET_ADMIN, capturing raw HTTP on a port (default :8080) and replaying it to an HTTP target (default http://localhost:7100) with --verbose; container restarts unless stopped. This is a same-host traffic mirroring setup ('模式2：命令行工具方式').
nodes.evidence: reference/plaud-org/goreplay/Jenkinsfile:5-17 params IMAGE_TAG/IMAGE_NAME/CONTAINER_NAME/INPUT_RAW=':8080'/OUTPUT_HTTP='http://localhost:7100'/EXTRA_ARGS='--verbose'/RESTART_CONTAINER=true; :50 gorArgs = "--input-raw ${INPUT_RAW} --output-http ${OUTPUT_HTTP}"; :58-67 docker run -d --cap-add=NET_RAW --cap-add=NET_ADMIN --network host --restart unless-stopped; :73 health check via docker ps | grep
nodes.notes: PROVEN_OFFICIAL_SOURCE for the mechanism; INFERRED for purpose. The Jenkinsfile never names prod/staging/test, which service listens on :8080, or what runs on :7100; both are overridable defaults. It therefore supports 'Plaud mirrors live HTTP traffic from one service to another instance' but not specifically 'prod into test'.
