nodes.behavior: JWT claims: the user token is a JWT; the only claim the docs name is `sub`, from which the SDK derives the BLE handshake token ('The handshake token is automatically parsed from the JWT sub field'; Android NiceBuildSdk.resolveHandshakeToken(userJwt)). Refreshing the user token in the SDK (setUserAccessToken) 'automatically updates the handshake token and refreshes the RSA key pair'.
nodes.notes: No `client_id` claim is documented. r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:118 says X-Client-Id is taken 'from the userAccessToken JWT client_id claim' (template source); docs say X-Client-Id is 'Your client_id, issued in the Portal' (openapi_transcription.json:148-153). Not contradictory, but the docs do not confirm such a claim exists.

nodes.behavior: Transcription API does NOT use either token; it authenticates with two API-key headers: X-Client-Id (client_id) and X-Client-Api-Key (api_key). The api_key is explicitly 'NOT your client_secret' — generated in Portal under App Settings > API Keys.
nodes.notes: Three credential kinds therefore exist: client_id+secret_key (Basic, backend only), user token (Bearer, mobile/SDK), client_id+api_key (headers, transcription).

nodes.behavior: POST /open/partner/sdk/bind and /unbind: Bearer user token, JSON {type (required; derived from SN prefix: 881 -> 'notepro', 882 -> 'notepins'), sn (required)}; 200 -> {type, sn, is_bind}; bind is idempotent for the same owner; bind 403 {code, message:'device already bound to another account'} when bound elsewhere; 404 unknown SN. Unbind: idempotent, 404 unknown SN; must be paired with SDK depair(clear:true) so cloud and local state stay in sync. Devices bind to only one application at a time.
nodes.notes: Binding is two-step: cloud bind (this API) then local BLE bind by the SDK which 'verifies and generates the key pair on-device' (openapi_binding.json:5). BLE-side details are FROZEN in docs/protocol-ledger.md; not re-derived here.

nodes.behavior: GET /open/partner/sdk/binding?type=&sn= (Bearer user token) -> {is_bind: boolean|null, bind_history: string[]}. is_bind tri-state: true = bound to ANOTHER account (recovery impossible), false = unbound, null = 'signed but never bound'. bind_history = previously bound client IDs newest first, one entry per bind event so duplicates occur (de-duplicate before Device Recovery); includes bindings made in other apps. Unknown SN -> bare 404 with no error body. Used to drive SDK Device Recovery (recoveryConnectBleDevice) when cloud and local bind state diverge and the device locks.
nodes.notes: 'signed but never bound' (null) implies a server-side sn-sign event precedes bind — consistent with r7's /sdk/sn-sign endpoint (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:91-97), which the public OpenAPI does not document.

nodes.behavior: 3-step S3 multipart flow, Bearer user token. (1) POST /open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls {filesize:int bytes (required), filetype:string (required, '"mp3" or "opus"')} -> {FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize (5242880), Parts:[{PartNumber (1-based), PresignedUrl}]}. (2) PUT raw bytes of each <=ChunkSize chunk directly to S3 (no auth) and read the ETag response header. (3) POST /open/partner/files/upload/complete-upload {file_id, upload_id, part_list:[{PartNumber, ETag}] (all required), filetype (required), file_md5 (optional hex MD5)} -> {FileId, FileType, DownloadUrl (valid ~24 h), FileMd5}. Pass DownloadUrl as file_url to Transcription. The File Upload API is optional: Transcription accepts any publicly accessible audio URL.
nodes.notes: Response keys are PascalCase (FileId, ChunkSize) while request keys are snake_case (file_id, part_list) — a naming split the docs preserve consistently. No max filesize and no error codes are documented for this API.

nodes.behavior: POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ (trailing slash) with X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key, JSON {file_url (required; 'M4A, MP3, WAV'), params?: {transcribe?: {language: BCP-47 or 'auto', default 'auto'; detection_level: 'segment'|'chapter', default 'segment'; model (transcription-model.json only)}, vad?: {decode_silence: bool, default false}, diarization?: {enabled: bool default false; return_embedding: bool default false}, hotwords (transcription.json only): comma-separated custom vocabulary string}} -> {transcription_id:'task_exec_xxx', status:'PENDING', data:{}}. nodes.behavior: Transcriptions processed by the API are retained 7 days by default (configurable on custom plans). Devices hold 64 GB local storage; builders may integrate devices only ('Full Data Custody': audio stays on device -> your app -> your services; app clears the device after sync) without sending audio to Plaud cloud. MCP HTTP mode: recording data passes through Plaud's US-hosted MCP server in transit only, not stored after the request.
nodes.notes: Retention of the uploaded AUDIO in Plaud S3 (beyond the 24 h DownloadUrl validity) is not stated anywhere.

nodes.behavior: PAYG along two meters: Connected Devices (max devices connected to your app in a month via the SDK) and Transcription Hours (hours transcribed via the API). Free tier per client: 50 connected devices + 300 transcription hours, the hours unlocked only after the first device connection. PAYG rates after free usage: $15 per device per month, $0.28 per transcription hour. Charged at end of month; payment failure -> 7-day grace period before service denial. PAYG has no device/transcription caps. Enterprise plans for HIPAA, volume discounts, dedicated support. Partner Program (bixgrow) for device-purchase tracking/incentives. End users need no Plaud App subscription.
nodes.notes: Nothing states how a 'connected device' is counted technically (cloud bind vs BLE connect vs sn-sign) — the SDK-side signal Plaud bills on is UNKNOWN.

nodes.behavior: Plaud Embedded supports only Note Pro (SN prefix 881, type 'notepro') and NotePin S (882, 'notepins'); Plaud Note and NotePin are NOT supported. Specs: Note Pro battery 30-50 h endurance, 4 MEMS + 1 VPU mics, dual-band Wi-Fi + BT, 64G, dual-mode calls+in-person; NotePin S 20 h, 2 MEMS, 64G, in-person. Max single-file recording duration 5 h on both.
nodes.notes: The 5 h device cap plus the '>5 h should be chunked' transcription note versus the '24 hr max recording' x-mint limit are three different numbers describing overlapping constraints.

nodes.behavior: MCP (@plaud-ai/mcp, Node>=20, OAuth browser login, tokens at ~/.plaud/tokens-mcp.json, local callback port 8199) tools: login, logout, get_current_user, list_files (query = case-insensitive keyword on name; date_from/date_to YYYY-MM-DD; page/page_size ignored when filters set), get_file, get_note (AI summary/action items/key topics), get_transcript (timestamps + speaker labels). Fields (list_files/get_file): id, name, created_at ISO8601, start_at ISO8601, duration (ms), serial_number. get_file-only: presigned_url (audio download, valid 24 h), source_list (transcript segments w/ timestamps+speakers), note_list (Markdown notes). Skills: plaud-browse/find/read/digest/followup/export. CLI (@plaud-ai/cli): login/logout/me; files (--page 1-1000, --page-size 10-100 default 20); recent [--days]; today; search <kw> [--from --to --max 50] = client-side case-insensitive keyword over recording names, scans up to 500 most recent; file/audio (24 h URL)/transcript/summary [-o]; version/update. plaud file adds start_at, serial_number, audio/transcript/summary availability booleans. Exit codes 0 ok, 1 args/unknown, 2 auth (AUTH_FAILED), 3 network, 4 timeout. Config ~/.plaud/cli.yaml {api_base default https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api, timeout 30000 ms}; env PLAUD_API_BASE, PLAUD_CLIENT_ID/PLAUD_CLI_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_CLIENT_SECRET, PLAUD_AUTH_URL, PLAUD_TOKEN_URL, PLAUD_REFRESH_URL. GA v1.0.0 on May 12 2026.
nodes.notes: MCP/CLI are a personal-account (consumer) surface; their underlying HTTP endpoints are not documented. The api_base under /developer/api suggests they ride the developer platform host, not api.plaud.ai (r7 surface C).

nodes.behavior: Plaud Embedded changelog: May 12 2026 v1.0.0 Developer Platform Beta Launch (iOS+Android SDK, starter app); May 18 2026 v1.0.5 MP3 export + WiFi fast transfer; Jun 29 2026 v1.0.6 live transfer speed, 0-100% export progress, batch download; Aug 3 2026 v1.0.11 Android SDK full parity (scan, connect, record, file list/sync/delete, settings, WiFi provisioning, fast transfer, OTA), MP3 over iOS WiFi; Aug 24 2026 v1.0.13 recoveryConnectBleDevice (reclaim device using historical user ID from bind history), connection-stage callbacks with failure reason, English-only SDK messages; Sep 14 2026 v1.0.14 'Workflow Query Deprecation — Deprecated workflow status and result query APIs on iOS and Android'. Advanced SDK pages: iOS 'PlaudWorkflowManager has been deprecated and will be removed in future SDK versions'; Android 'The workflow methods and models have been deprecated'.
nodes.notes: This is the most plausible explanation for r7 surface A's /api/workflows/submit|status|result being in the SDK binary but absent from every documented API: the workflow surface is the SDK's own (deprecated) AI path, superseded by the documented /ai/transcriptions API. Note the changelog deprecates the status/result QUERY methods; it does not say submit is deprecated.

nodes.behavior: The docs themselves acknowledge a second, undocumented '/api/...' service used by the SDK: (a) 'NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice(...) / unbindDevice(...) are not the cloud bind documented in the Android SDK reference. They post to a different service (/api/devices/bind) with a different credential. For the documented flow, call developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind directly with the user token.' (b) 'Android's firmware version check queries GET /api/sdk/latest-version with an Authorization header, while iOS uses the partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature.'
nodes.notes: This is Plaud stating that surface A (/api/...) and surface B (/developer/api/open/partner/...) are different services with different credentials — bearing on r7's open question (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:130-137). It remains a claim; no runtime evidence.

nodes.behavior: Four-party architecture: (1) partner backend services exchange client_id+client_secret for partner token and mint user tokens; (2) partner mobile app initializes the SDK with the user token + regional domain, binds device (cloud bind + BLE bind), syncs audio over BLE (default) or WiFi fast transfer (~10x faster); (3) Plaud device stores encrypted audio (64 GB), bound to exactly one app so stolen-device data stays inaccessible; (4) Plaud cloud: token issuance, device registry, optional S3 upload, transcription. Audio is synced 'from Plaud devices to your backend' and only the file_url is passed to Plaud cloud for transcription.
nodes.notes: The docs put partner token minting on the partner backend; the playground and starter apps instead put the user token straight into the mobile app config (plaud-embedded_android-starter-app.md:68-78), so real deployments may skip the backend hop.

nodes.text: Whether the requested user-token expires_in is honored verbatim, capped, or has a maximum; and whether user tokens can be refreshed at all (no refresh_token in UserTokenResponse, openapi_auth.json:229-247).
The partner refresh_token lifetime and whether refresh rotates the refresh_token (example shows a refresh_token in the refresh response, openapi_auth.json:96-101).

What exactly increments the billable 'Connected Devices' meter (cloud bind, BLE connect, sn-sign, or first sync) — the docs define it only as 'devices ... connected to via the Embedded SDK' (plaud-embedded_billing.md:13, :17-19).
How is_bind becomes null ('signed but never bound', openapi_binding.json:243) — implies /sdk/sn-sign writes to the registry, but sn-sign is not in the public spec.
Whether plaud-transcribe-1 (playground) is an alias of plaud-fast-whisper, a newer model, or invalid against the enum in transcription-model.json.

Whether 'hotwords' (transcription.json only) and 'model' (transcription-model.json only) can be sent together; the specs are two snapshots of one endpoint with no version marker (both info.version 0.0.1).
Retention of uploaded AUDIO in Plaud S3 after the 24 h DownloadUrl expires (only transcription results have a stated 7-day retention).
Whether FAILURE/REVOKED carry an error message/code in data; no error schema is documented for the transcription or file APIs.
Whether the POST /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ trailing slash is significant (every doc sample includes it; the GET has none).
Which underlying HTTP API the MCP/CLI tools call and why their default api_base (platform.plaud.ai/developer/api) is region-less while every partner spec is region-prefixed.
Whether the 'Workflow Query Deprecation' (Sep 14 2026) also removes /api/workflows/submit or only the status/result queries; the changelog names only the query APIs.

The dangling anchor auth-api-overview#find-your-region (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:115) — a 'Find your region' section appears to have been removed or never published, so the official regional-host discovery step is missing.

WORKFLOWS: r7 surface A lists POST /api/workflows/submit, GET /api/workflows/{id}/status, GET /api/workflows/{id}/result in the SDK jar (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:78-81) and surface D says python-plaud-ai's workflows/* 'mirrors docs.plaud.ai' (:164). The docs fetched 2026-09-23 contain NO workflows endpoint anywhere; the only documented AI surface is /open/partner/ai/transcriptions/ with X-Client-Id/X-Client-Api-Key (openapi_transcription.json:19-144). The changelog v1.0.14 Sep 14 2026 'Deprecated workflow status and result query APIs on iOS and Android' (plaud-embedded_changelog.md:7-11) and the advanced pages ('PlaudWorkflowManager has been deprecated', plaud-embedded_advanced-ios-sdk.md:64; 'workflow methods and models ... deprecated', plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:64) indicate the binary's workflow surface is a superseded SDK path. Both sides reported; r7's characterization of D as 'the documented form' is not supported by the current docs (may reflect an older doc version).

DEFAULT HOST: r7 records the SDK ServerEnvironment default US_PROD = https://platform-jp.plaud.ai with alternates platform.plaud.cn, dev-api-us-test.plaud.work, platform-beta.plaud.ai (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:19). Docs state US = platform-us.plaud.ai is the default region and JP = platform-jp.plaud.ai (plaud-embedded_data-retention.md:47-50; openapi_*.json:8-17); the SDK docs tell integrators to pass customDomain 'platform-us.plaud.ai' (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:104). The SDK enum (per r7) contains no platform-us, platform-eu or platform-sg host and the docs list no .cn, beta or dev-test host.

BIND ENDPOINT FAMILY: r7 lists POST /api/devices/bind|unbind (Bearer api_token, BYTECODE_PROVEN) and asks whether /api/... aliases the partner API (r7:73-76, :130-137). Docs: bind is POST /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind with Bearer user token (openapi_binding.json:24-80), AND Plaud's own note states 'NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice(...)/unbindDevice(...) are not the cloud bind ... They post to a different service (/api/devices/bind) with a different credential' (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:440-442). Docs thus claim the two are distinct services — an OFFICIAL_DOC claim, not runtime proof; r7's UNKNOWN stands at runtime level.

VERSION CHECK: r7 lists GET /api/sdk/latest-version (binary, Bearer) and GET .../partner/sdk/version/latest (template, Bearer user token) (r7:83-86, :124). Docs: 'Android's firmware version check queries GET /api/sdk/latest-version with an Authorization header, while iOS uses the partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature' (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:274-276). Docs add a platform split and an X-Device-Signature auth on the iOS partner path that r7 attributes only to /partner/sdk/metadata (r7:111-114); neither version endpoint appears in the public OpenAPI.

UPLOAD PATHS: r7 binary uses POST /api/files/upload-s3/generate-presigned-urls and complete-upload with Bearer api_token (r7:60-66); docs document only /developer/api/open/partner/files/upload/generate-presigned-urls and complete-upload with Bearer user token (openapi_file.json:19-139). Same class-name (GeneratePresignedUrlsRequest) but different path prefix and credential; docs give the JSON field names r7 could not decompile (filesize, filetype, FileId, UploadId, ChunkSize, Parts, file_id, upload_id, part_list, file_md5).

TOKEN CHAIN: r7 surface A is a 3-hop chain /api/oauth/sdk-token (Bearer Base64(appKey:appSecret)) -> /api/sdk/api-token -> api_token (r7:34-51); surface D uses POST platform.plaud.ai/api/oauth/api-token (r7:164). Docs document a different 2-hop chain: Basic base64(client_id:secret_key) -> /developer/api/oauth/partner/access-token (with refresh) -> /developer/api/open/partner/users/access-token (openapi_auth.json). None of /api/oauth/sdk-token, /api/sdk/api-token, /api/oauth/api-token appear in the docs.

UNDOCUMENTED PARTNER ENDPOINTS: r7 surface B has POST .../partner/sdk/sn-sign, sn-verify, gen-key (returns RSA private key), metadata (X-Device-Signature) (r7:91-114). The public OpenAPI (openapi_binding.json) documents only bind/unbind/binding. The SDK prose pages do reference sn-sign, RSA key-pair generation and PartnerApiManager (plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:59, :338, :401, :430-437), and binding's is_bind=null 'signed but never bound' presupposes sn-sign, so the docs corroborate their existence without contracting them.

X-CLIENT-ID SOURCE: r7 says X-Client-Id is 'from the userAccessToken JWT client_id claim' (r7:118, template code). Docs say X-Client-Id is 'Your client_id, issued in the Portal' (openapi_transcription.json:148-153) and the only JWT claim they name is sub (plaud-embedded_ios-sdk.md:109; plaud-embedded_advanced-android-sdk.md:139). Not contradictory, but the client_id claim is unconfirmed by docs.

CONSUMER SURFACE C vs MCP/CLI: r7 surface C is https://api.plaud.ai (community clients) (r7:21, :139-160). The official CLI's default api_base is https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api (plaud-mcp-cli_cli.md:145) — Plaud's own personal-data tools ride the developer-platform host, not api.plaud.ai. Which backend serves MCP/CLI data is otherwise undocumented.

nodes.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK(context, userAccessToken, customDomain) initialises the singleton; customDomain is 'domain only, no https://' and 'All SDK network requests use this domain'; initSDK 'fetches the key pair asynchronously' (gen-key) so callers must poll NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() before connecting.
nodes.notes: Ledger §4.5 / r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:97-103 agree the RSA pair comes from POST /developer/api/open/partner/sdk/gen-key and that isPartnerDataReady gates connect (BYTECODE_PROVEN path, CLOUD_OBSERVED endpoint).

nodes.behavior: sdk.permission.PermissionManager requests BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION on API 31+, and BLUETOOTH, BLUETOOTH_ADMIN, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION on API ≤ 30; 'it asks for location on Android 12+ as well'. onResult receives true only when every requested permission was granted.
nodes.notes: Starter app page says location is needed only 'on Android 11 and below' (plaud-embedded_android-starter-app.md:227) — internal doc inconsistency.

nodes.behavior: Binding is documented as two steps: (1) 'Local bind over BLE, where the Embedded SDK runs the encrypted handshake and generates the key-pair on the device'; (2) 'Cloud bind' via POST https://<domain>/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/bind {type, sn} with Bearer user token, called by the app after bleBind(status=0); 403 = already bound to another account; re-bind to same owner is idempotent. Preconditions for connectBleDevice: RSA key pair arrived AND SN signed via NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn), read 'during the pre-handshake'.
nodes.notes: CONTRADICTS ledger §4.4 ('There is no BLE bind message'; bleBind fires from btStatusChange(CONNECTED) ← sync_time success), §4.5 (key pair is cloud-issued incl. private key; SDK never calls KeyPairGenerator) and §4.6 (below advertised portVersion 20 there is no encryption and no signature — token only). Both sides reported in doc_vs_code_contradictions.

nodes.behavior: bleConnectState(state): 1 = GATT link up, handshake still pending (explicitly 'not connection success'); 0 = disconnected; 2 = connection failed. bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone): 'status == 0 is the real connection success'. blePenState(state, privacy, keyState, uDisk) reported after the handshake.
nodes.notes: Ledger §14 (run 4) proves protVersion and timezone are both loaded from the l3 timezone byte; the docs do not caveat this.

nodes.behavior: bleConnectStage(sn: String?, stage: String, detail: String?) is 'the only way to see which layer refused a rejected connection'; sn may be null before SN known. stage ∈ {start, gatt_connect, set_notify, set_battery_notify, read_battery, set_data_notify, pre_handshake, send_rsa_public, first_handshake, two_handshake, handshake_get_ssn, change_handshake_timeout, sync_time}; detail ∈ {ok, old_protocol_ok, status_<n> (status_1 = token mismatch), sn_signature_empty, sn_signature_invalid, user_rsa_public_key_empty, bind_token_empty, send_fail}. Before SDK 1.0.13 all collapsed into bleConnectState(2); 1.0.13 forwards it through the facade.
nodes.notes: Stage list matches ledger §4.1 (DIRECT) exactly. old_protocol_ok is the legacy (pv<20) path label observed live in §14 runs 1/3/4; docs list it without explaining that an unencrypted path exists.

nodes.behavior: 'Plaud devices can only be bound to one application at a time (tied to your Partner Token).' Unbind before uninstalling; otherwise the device cannot be bound to another app or the Plaud app.
nodes.notes: Cloud-side policy claim; not testable from bytecode. Ledger §4.6 notes the device decides token acceptance.

nodes.behavior: Standard unbind = cloud POST sdk/unbind (idempotent no-op if already unbound, no BLE needed) + BLE depair(clear=false) → bleDepair(status) (0 = depaired) → disconnect(). 'Because an out-of-range or unresponsive device never answers, pair the callback with a short timeout that disconnects anyway' (sample: 3 000 ms). clear=true 'also clears the SDK's stored connection/bond state'; keep false during recovery. No-arg depair() is equivalent to depair(false).
nodes.notes: Ledger has no depair wire message recorded; 'depair changes the MAC — rescan' (android-sdk.md:423) has no bytecode counterpart (see unexplained).

nodes.behavior: Device Recovery applies when cloud and local bind state are out-of-sync ('on Android this usually surfaces as a bleConnectState(2) connect failure after a ~10s timeout'). Only when GET sdk/binding reports is_bind false or null (true = owned by another account, SDK cannot override). bind_history = client IDs newest first, one entry per bind event ('50+ duplicates of a single ID is normal' — dedupe). For each id: recoveryConnectBleDevice(bleDevice, historicalUserId) 'uses that ID as the handshake token and connects with force-clear, so the firmware wipes its stale key material'; current user's SN signature and RSA material are reused; SDK 'restores the current user's handshake identity when the attempt ends'. On bleBind(status==0) → depair(false) → bleDepair → disconnect() + startScan() ('depair changes the MAC — rescan') → connectBleDevice(fresh) as current user. bleConnectState 0/2 while awaiting handshake = id refused, try next. historicalUserId 'Accepts either the raw client_user_id or its 32-hex form'.
nodes.notes: Compare ledger §14 / r7-s12: SDK normalises by removePrefix('client_user_') + drop '-', aborts on empty (bleConnectState(2)), warns if length≠32, passes isForceClear=true which only selects 0xFE20 (inert below pv 20, observed); FE20 device effect is UNKNOWN (U10). Doc code comment at :417 ('if (status != 0) return // this ID matched the firmware lock') reads inverted relative to :245 ('0 = handshake complete').

nodes.behavior: 'Plaud devices will record up to 5 hours. Recordings longer should be broken up.' getFileList() → bleFileList(List<BleFile>). exportAudio(sessionId, outputDir, format: AudioExportFormat {PCM|WAV|OPUS|MP3}, channels: Int (1=mono, optional overload), callback: AudioExporter.ExportCallback). MP3 recommended ('accepted directly by the transcription upload API'). ExportCallback: onProgress(progress 0-100 'download bytes', message), onComplete(outputFile), onError(error), optional onStageChanged(ExportStage DOWNLOADING → TRANSCODING). Facade handles 'download, caching, E2EE decrypt, and transcode'. Callbacks arrive on SDK internal threads, not main.
nodes.notes: Ledger §8: chain syncFile → t7.d() → o4 pass-through → AudioExporter, sniff-based (PLAUD.AI header ≥512 B → ChaCha decrypt; 'OggS' → Ogg). 5 h limit has no bytecode counterpart.

nodes.behavior: ~10x faster than BLE. setDeviceWiFi(open=true) → bleWiFiOpen(status, ssid, password, url) → startWifiTransfer(userId, WifiTransferCallback): Boolean (false if session could not open) → state NONE → CONNECTING → CONNECTED → HANDSHAKING → READY; 'No file command works before READY' → getWifiAgent()?.getFileList() → onFileListReceived(List<WifiFileInfo>) → exportAudioViaWiFi(same args as exportAudio, same ExportCallback) → endWiFiTransfer() (only this also closes the hotspot over BLE; stopWifiTransfer() leaves hotspot open draining battery). getWifiAgent() is null until an agent exists. isWifiTransferActive() checks session. deleteFiles(List<Long>) is 'the only batch delete in the SDK' → onFileDeleteCompleted. downloadFile()/downloadAllFiles() 'write undecrypted .opus bytes straight to disk'. onTransferProgress(sessionId, progress 0-100, speed KB/s).
nodes.notes: Ledger §7 (SOURCE-DERIVED, NOT IMPLEMENTED): pen raises WPA2 SoftAP (SSID 'PLAUD'+last4 SN, pass = last 8 SN chars), phone runs WebSocket server on 8081, pen dials in; opcode 10 OpenWiFi / 13 CloseWiFi on BLE side. WifiFileInfo fields (fileName/duration/timestamp) exceed the recovered 10-byte GetFileList record [sessionId][fileSize][u16 scene].

nodes.behavior: Three calls: checkFirmwareUpdate(cb) → downloadFirmware(info, cb) → installFirmware(file, info, cb); flow 'version query → download → MD5 verify → CRC → BLE packet push → device restart → reconnect'. FirmwareUpdateInfo{hasUpdate, currentVersion, isForceUpdate, versionResponse: DeviceVersionResponse(latest version, download URL, MD5, release notes)}. UpdateProgress{progress 0-100, message, detail, transferPhase: FirmwareTransferPhase}. FirmwareTransferPhase ∈ {TRANSFERRING, TRANSFER_COMPLETE_WAITING, DEVICE_RESTARTING, UPGRADE_COMPLETE, TRANSFER_FAILED, UPGRADE_FAILED}. FirmwareDownloadResult{success, file, md5Valid, error}; FirmwareInstallResult{success, error}. SimpleFirmwareUpdateCallback has empty defaults. 'Firmware updates will wipe recordings.' Android version check = GET /api/sdk/latest-version with Authorization header (iOS: partner endpoint with X-Device-Signature). Low-level: appFotaPush(filePath, fromVersion, toVersion, thirdVersion, otaPushListener), isFotaPushing(), interruptFotaPush(), getSyncOtaFileInfo(), appGetThirdVersion(); FirmwareUpdateManager composes the flow.
nodes.notes: Closure report: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (0x1021, init 0xFFFF) for the OTA whole-file path (BYTECODE_PROVEN); latest-version endpoint CLOUD_OBSERVED (r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:83).

nodes.behavior: gen-key and sn-sign are POST …/sdk/gen-key and …/sdk/sn-sign with 'Authorization: Bearer <user token>', driven by PartnerApiManager.generateRsaKeyPair / signDeviceSn. deviceType from SN prefix: 881 → notepro, 882 → notepins. 'The SN signature is stored in memory only — there is no Keystore-backed cache and no persistence across process death. Every fresh launch needs a live sn-sign call before its first connect, so the device requires network reachability at that moment.' RSA key pair IS persisted, 'wrapped by an AES master key in the Android Keystore, and is what feeds audio E2EE decryption'; NiceBuildSdk.getSecurePrivateKey() returns PEM; clearPartnerData() drops it. handshakeToken = user JWT 'sub' claim via NiceBuildSdk.resolveHandshakeToken(userJwt).
nodes.notes: Ledger §4.5 (DIRECT): gen-key returns public_key AND private_key PEM; sn-sign opaque base64; token 32 hex with pad/truncate. Consistent. §4.3: private keys parsed as PKCS#8 PEM.

nodes.behavior: IBleAgent = TntAgent.getInstant().bleAgent, 165 methods; every command takes AgentCallback.OnRequest{onRequestResult(success, code, msg)} + AgentCallback.OnResponse<T>{onResponse(rsp)}; 'OnRequest fires when the command is written to the device; OnResponse fires when the device answers. A successful OnRequest with no OnResponse means the device accepted the command but never replied.' BleAgentListener registered via TntAgent.getInstant().addBleAgentListeners/removeBleAgentListeners; 29 members, 27 required. workflow methods/models deprecated. NiceBuildSdk.bindDevice/unbindDevice post to /api/devices/bind with a different credential and are NOT the documented cloud bind.
nodes.notes: Ledger §4.4: 'The unrelated cloud bind (POST /api/devices/bind) is never called by the SDK' — consistent (exists, unused internally). Closure report: no transport ACK, application responses serve as protocol responses — consistent with the OnRequest/OnResponse semantics.

nodes.behavior: Device settings are exposed only on IBleAgent as get/set pairs: BackLightTime, BackLightBrightness, Language, RecScene, RecMode, openVAD, VadSensitivity, VpuGain, MICGain, VpuCLK, BatteryMode, getAudioChannel, isOggAudio, isNoNsAgc, AutoRecord, AutoStopRecord, AutoPowerOff, AutoSync, AutoDeleteRecordFile, SaveRAWFile, FindMyState, IBeaconWakeup, SwitchHandlerId, BleDeviceName, LedStatus, AlarmRec, setPrivacy, setActive, restoreFactorySettings, plus generic getCommonParams/setCommonParams/commonSettings. No value ranges, units or defaults are documented for any setting. Facade surfaces only bleMicGain(gain) and bleDeviceName(name) callbacks.
nodes.notes: Mapping to ledger §5.12 CommonType wire values given in api_surface (20 of 21 names correspond; WIFI_CHANNEL has no dedicated documented method). Ledger: which values real firmware reports is UNKNOWN (U22); emulator values are POLICY.

nodes.behavior: PlaudDeviceAgent documents no start/stop recording method; recording control is IBleAgent only: startRecord(scene, …), stopRecord, recordPause(sessionId, …), recordResume(sessionId, …), startImmediateRecord, stopImmediateRecord, startSyncRecord. The facade re-emits bleRecordStart(sessionId, start, status, scene, startTime, reason), bleRecordStop(sessionId, reason, fileExist, fileSize), bleRecordPause(same), bleRecordResume(sessionId, start, status, scene, startTime).

'There is no format conversion and no decryption at this layer.'

nodes.behavior: Starter app: minSdk 21, compileSdk 34, JDK 17, physical arm64-v8a/armeabi-v7a device only; local.properties keys PLAUD_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN (required), PLAUD_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_API_KEY (transcription only); default namespace/applicationId com.plaud.template; Play Store requires compileSdk 35; bump versionCode every upload; $25 one-time Play fee; Bluetooth permission declaration (+ location on Android 11 and below).
nodes.notes: Product/packaging constraints, not protocol.

nodes.text: 'depair changes the MAC — rescan' (android-sdk.md:423): no depair wire message, and no MAC-rotation behaviour, is recorded in protocol-ledger.md or the closure report; DEVICE_REQUIRED.
'~10x faster than BLE' (android-sdk.md:522) and 'up to 5 hours' per recording (android-sdk.md:465): no bytecode or runtime counterpart; product claims only.

Transfer-speed reporting on BLE: plaud-embedded_changelog.md:35-37 announces 'Live download speed reporting for WiFi fast transfer and BLE transfers', but the Android AudioExporter.ExportCallback (android-sdk.md:874-888) exposes no speed argument; only WifiTransferCallback.onTransferProgress carries speed (KB/s). Where BLE speed surfaces on Android is undocumented (possibly the onProgress `message` string).
WifiTransferCallback.onError(code, message) and AgentCallback.OnRequest code: no error-code table is documented anywhere in the three files.

Setting value ranges: none of the 21 CommonType settings (nor LED/alarm/name/privacy) has a documented range, unit or default; ledger §5.12 likewise marks real-firmware values UNKNOWN (U22) — the emulator's DEFAULT_COMMON_SETTINGS are POLICY.
WIFI_CHANNEL (wire 21) has no dedicated IBleAgent get/set method in the docs' settings list; presumably only reachable via getCommonParams/setCommonParams/commonSettings.
PlaudDeviceAgent.deleteFile(...) is implied by the bleDeleteFile description (android-sdk.md:845) but its signature is never given.

The seven onWifiSync* listener callbacks (android-sdk.md:850) have no documented signatures and no documented triggering methods on PlaudDeviceAgent (IBleAgent's getWifiList/getWifiInfo/setSyncWifi/deleteWifiInfo/testWifiInfo/testWifiResult at advanced-android-sdk.md:220-221 are the likely drivers).
Permission scope inconsistency between pages: android-sdk.md:169 says location is requested on Android 12+ as well; android-starter-app.md:227 says location is needed only on Android 11 and below.

'The SDK restores the current user's handshake identity when the attempt ends' (android-sdk.md:409): no corresponding step is identified in the ledger's recovery trace (r7-s12 lines 36-42 end at t3.a(...)).

ADV:341 claims bleConnectStage has been 'a default-bodied member of BleAgentListener since the first public release' while ADV:289 counts 27 of 29 members required and ADV:315 marks commonSettingNotify as the (only named) default — the second default member is not named.
IBleAgent 'exposes 165 methods' (advanced-android-sdk.md:80) — not verified against the AAR here; the docs list ~110 by name.

refreshRecordState and getSnSignature (named in the task) do not appear in any fetched doc; X-Device-Signature appears only as an iOS aside (advanced-android-sdk.md:275) and in r7/cloud-endpoint-inventory.md:112 for POST …/sdk/metadata (computation site UNKNOWN). The Android PartnerApiManager.postDeviceMetadata(signature, request) takes the signature as a caller-supplied string, so how an Android app obtains it is undocumented.

bleBind.protVersion: DOC (android-sdk.md:244,283,827) presents bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone) with protVersion as a protocol-version parameter and no caveat. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §14 lines 1468-1475, run 4; final-closure-report.md:143-147, RUNTIME_PROVEN): the facade passes status=0 literally and loads BOTH protVersion and timezone from q.n = the l3 timezone byte (offset 6), not from l3 portVersion; setting emulator l3 tz=5 produced bleBind protVersion=5 tz=5. The true port version is never surfaced through bleBind.

Meaning of 'local bind': DOC (android-sdk.md:180) 'Local bind over BLE, where the Embedded SDK runs the encrypted handshake and generates the key-pair on the device'; (android-sdk.md:176) 'Binding a Plaud device generates a key-pair using the user token'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.4 lines 341-349, SOURCE-DERIVED): 'There is no BLE bind message'; bleBind fires from btStatusChange(CONNECTED) ← sync_time success, gated on handshake status 0 + opcode-9 battery (pv≥5) + syncTime, with SYNC_TIME_FAIL (-8) if the last never lands. §4.5 (DIRECT): the RSA key pair is issued by POST …/sdk/gen-key (public AND private key PEM); 'The SDK never calls KeyPairGenerator for this'. Nothing is generated on the device.

Encryption is unconditional in the docs but portVersion-gated in code: DOC (android-sdk.md:176-180; advanced-android-sdk.md:328 lists old_protocol_ok without explanation) implies every connect runs the encrypted handshake. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.2, §4.6 lines 266-276, 362-390; §14 lines 1462-1466): only advertised portVersion ≥ 20 runs the RSA pre-handshake and sealed channel; below 20, q.b0 goes straight to first_handshake whose only precondition is a non-empty token, no signature, no key, no cryptography (RUNTIME_PROVEN against the emulator at pv 7: 'old_protocol_ok → sync_time → bind 0').

Recovery force-clear semantics: DOC (android-sdk.md:409) 'connects with force-clear, so the firmware wipes its stale key material'; (android-sdk.md:350) 'the recovery handshake has already force-cleared the device's key material'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §2 lines 180-206, §9 U10, §14 lines 1465-1466; r7/r7-s12-k3-runtime-capture.md:36-48): isForceClear only selects marker 0xFE20 (PRE_HANDSHAKE_AND_CLEAR) vs 0xFE10, consumed by the pre-handshake; 'isForceClear is inert below portVersion 20 (predicted; observed)' — no marker frame was written; 'The meaning of isForceClear (0xFE20 vs 0xFE10)' is UNKNOWN (U10), settled only by hardware. The wipe claim is a doc assertion with no bytecode/runtime counterpart.

Recovery token handling: DOC (android-sdk.md:444) historicalUserId 'Accepts either the raw client_user_id or its 32-hex form'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §14 runs 1-3 lines 1446-1453; r7-s12 write-up lines 36-42): the SDK strips prefix 'client_user_' and '-', aborts with bleConnectState(2) on empty, warns when length ≠ 32 ('lower layer pads with zeros / truncates'), then k3 right-pads with '0' to 32 (pv≥9) or 16 chars — run 3 silently TRUNCATED a 32-char id to 16 at pv 7. Also DOC (android-sdk.md:409) says 'nothing has to be signed for the historical user' and the SDK 'restores the current user's handshake identity' — the ledger confirms no cloud call on this path (t3.a with no resolveHandshakeToken) but records nothing about an identity-restore step.

Recovery sample-code comment inversion (doc-internal): android-sdk.md:417 'if (status != 0) return // this ID matched the firmware lock' vs :245 '0 = handshake complete' and :417 flow (status==0 → depair). The comment labels the non-zero branch as the match while the code treats status==0 as the match.

PlaudDeviceAgentListener enumeration: DOC (android-sdk.md:822-851; advanced-android-sdk.md:290 '32 members') lists 24 table callbacks + 7 onWifiSync* + bleConnectStage = 32 and never mentions a time-sync callback. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §5.2 lines 469-472, DIRECT): syncTime$1.onCallback forwards n7.c() as the first argument of PlaudDeviceAgentListener.bleTimeSync(timezone, stamp). Either the docs' 32 count omits bleTimeSync or one listed member is not a listener member.

WifiFileInfo metadata: DOC (android-sdk.md:931) WifiFileInfo carries sessionId, fileName, fileSize, duration (ms), timestamp (epoch seconds), scene. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §7 lines 1075-1080, SOURCE-DERIVED): Wi-Fi GetFileList (type 11) returns JSON {uid,status,count,offset} plus 10-byte records [u32le sessionId][u32le fileSize][u16le scene] — no fileName, duration or timestamp on the wire. Those fields must be derived client-side or come from an unrecovered field; the doc's 'more per-file metadata than BleFile' is not supported by the recovered record layout.

bleData payload: DOC (android-sdk.md:842) 'A chunk of streaming audio/PCM bytes'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §8 / final-closure-report.md Audio): o4 is a pure pass-through, so DATA payloads equal the stored file byte-for-byte (Opus/Ogg, possibly PLAUD.AI-encrypted) — not PCM; PCM only exists after AudioExporter transcode.

syncFileStart end=0 semantics: DOC (advanced-android-sdk.md:252-254) 'End byte offset. 0 transfers to the end of the file.' CODE (protocol-ledger.md §9 U14): 'Whether y6's end is inclusive or exclusive, and whether 0 formally means EOF' is UNKNOWN — no shipped code sends a non-zero end and no capture exists. The doc statement is a claim the record cannot confirm.

downloadFile output shape: DOC (android-sdk.md:604) IWifiTransferAgent.downloadFile/downloadAllFiles 'write undecrypted .opus bytes straight to disk'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §9 U20; final-closure-report.md Audio): which of {plain, PLAUD.AI-encrypted} × {Ogg, raw Opus} real firmware emits is UNKNOWN; selection is sniff-based at export time. The doc asserts both 'undecrypted' and '.opus' as fixed.

Locked-device timeout: DOC (android-sdk.md:357) 'bleConnectState(2) connect failure after a ~10s timeout'. CODE: the ledger records no 10 s connect/handshake timeout constant (only change_handshake_timeout as a stage name §4.1, 'retried a few times' §4.4, and the 5 000 ms file-sync stall timeout §5.8/5.9). Unverified rather than contradicted.

Bind-to-one-app enforcement locus: DOC (android-sdk.md:298; android-starter-app.md:141) 'can only be bound to one application at a time (tied to your Partner Token)'. CODE (protocol-ledger.md §4.6): on the legacy path 'the host sends a token, and the DEVICE returns a status. The secret belongs to the device'; R7-S12 emulator accepted any token as HARNESS POLICY. Whether real firmware enforces a single-owner lock (status_1) is DEVICE_REQUIRED (no contradiction, but the docs' cloud-tied framing is not what the bytecode shows — the device-side check is local).

nodes.behavior: Capacitor Android plugin attaches a raw BleAgentListener (transport layer) and deliberately stubs the device-state/settings callbacks it does not forward: rssiChange, batteryLevelUpdate, chargingStatusChange, deviceOpRecordStart/Stop/Pause/Resume, deviceOpStorageRsp, deviceStatusRsp, deviceStatusDetailed, deviceLogSync*, deviceFotaResult, deviceFotaThirdVersion, deviceWifiSyncStartRsp, deviceSwitchWifiMode, motorStatus, stickAngles, deviceNewFeature, sendMoreFailDisconnect, mtuChange. This is the most complete in-source inventory of what the transport offers and the wrappers drop (battery/charging/storage/status/OTA result/WiFi mode/motor/angles).
nodes.notes: Only bleConnectFail, bleConnectStage, btStatusChange, handshakeWaitSure, scanFail are forwarded (as Android-only events).

nodes.behavior: Every wrapper receives bleBind(sn, status, protVersion, timezone) from the SDK but emits only {sn, status, protVersion}; the timezone argument is dropped on all six native implementations.

Cited, not re-derived.

nodes.behavior: Capacitor shell loads a remote HTTPS origin rather than bundled assets: server.url='https://plaud-capacitor-demo.vercel.app', cleartext:false, webDir:'public' (ignored). Consequence stated in README: the app runs whatever is deployed to Vercel; native changes need Xcode/Gradle rebuild.
nodes.notes: Doc's copy of the config uses appId 'ai.plaud.capacitordemo' (web-app-wrapper.md:307-319) while the repo uses 'ai.plaud.pwademo'.

nodes.behavior: Split of responsibilities: WebView runs React page.tsx, the registerPlugin('PlaudSdk') proxy (lib/plaud-sdk.ts) and app/transcription-runner.ts (the only code that touches raw audio bytes). Native runs PlaudSdkPlugin (SDK init/scan/connect/list/export, file read, S3 PUT). Server (Next.js route handlers, Node runtime) mints tokens and proxies Plaud APIs. Route handlers never see audio bytes; multipart PUTs go native -> S3.
nodes.notes: lib/ is reserved for server-only modules; runner lives under app/ on purpose (README.md:341-347).

nodes.behavior: The plugin is app-local (SwiftPM package with three .binaryTarget xcframeworks; Java class in the app module against libs/plaud-sdk.aar), so it is not in Capacitor's packageClassList and must be registered by hand: iOS bridge?.registerPluginInstance(PlaudSdkPlugin()) in MainViewController.capacitorDidLoad(); Android registerPlugin(PlaudSdkPlugin.class) before super.onCreate().
nodes.notes: Docs web-app-wrapper.md:154-220 match this.

nodes.behavior: User token path: page.tsx useSWR POSTs {user_id: USER_ID='jackmu'} to `${window.location.origin}/api/user-token`; server mintUserToken() does POST /oauth/partner/access-token with Basic base64(PLAUD_CLIENT_ID:PLAUD_SECRET_KEY) then POST /open/partner/users/access-token with Bearer partner token and {user_id, expires_in:86400}; returns {access_token, expires_in}; client keeps it in SWR state only (no localStorage/sessionStorage) and passes it across the bridge in PlaudSdk.initSDK({userAccessToken, customDomain:'platform-us.plaud.ai', userId}); native calls PlaudDeviceAgent.shared.initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:). The same access_token is later sent in the JSON body of /api/transcription/presign and /complete, which forward it as Authorization: Bearer.
nodes.notes: initSDK is called lazily on first Scan tap (initedRef guard), not at mount.

nodes.behavior: POST /api/user-token: no authentication, no origin/CSRF check, no rate limit; accepts any non-empty user_id string and mints a Plaud user token for it using the partner secret -- a token-minting oracle for anyone who can reach the deployed origin. Logs the user id. Errors: 400 bad JSON/user_id, 502 PlaudApiError (message includes upstream status), 500 generic.
nodes.notes: Demo code; README/CLAUDE.md frame the route's purpose as keeping credentials server-side, not as an auth boundary.

nodes.behavior: POST /api/transcription/presign and /complete: unauthenticated proxies that take the caller-supplied access_token from the JSON body and relay it as Bearer; validate filesize>0 and filetype in {mp3,opus}; /complete validates part_list shape and optional file_md5. Both console.log the full upstream response (presigned S3 URLs and DownloadUrl are written to server logs).
nodes.notes: filetype restricted to mp3|opus although exportAudio can produce pcm/wav.

nodes.behavior: POST /api/transcription/submit and GET /api/transcription/status/[id]: unauthenticated; submit accepts any file_url string and optional params and spends the partner credentials (X-Client-Id / X-Client-Api-Key from PLAUD_CLIENT_ID / PLAUD_API_KEY) on it; status accepts any id. Both log full task payloads. No allow-list on file_url host, no rate limiting.
nodes.notes: Anyone reaching the origin can submit arbitrary public URLs for transcription billed to the partner.

nodes.behavior: readFile (base64 of an exported file; accepts raw path, file:// or a capacitor://.../_capacitor_file_/... URL) and putBinary (native PUT of base64 body to arbitrary URL returning {status, etag}; sets Content-Type only if caller passes one, Android explicitly blanks it) exist solely because the remote-origin WebView's CORS check blocks fetch() of convertFileSrc URLs and browser PUTs to S3 presigned URLs (and ETag would not be readable without bucket ExposeHeaders).
nodes.notes: putBinary is an open native PUT primitive callable from any JS running in the WebView (no URL allow-list). RN README says these shims were 'not ported' because RN has no WebView/CORS constraint (modules/plaud-sdk/README.md:113-117).

nodes.behavior: All three Android implementations perform work the iOS ones do not: (1) NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl('https://'+customDomain) before PlaudDeviceAgent.initSDK because the SDK's Partner API Retrofit client 'hardcodes https://platform-jp.plaud.ai and does not follow customDomain'; (2) before connect, wait up to 10 s for NiceBuildSdk.isPartnerDataReady() (RSA key pair fetched asynchronously by initSDK); (3) NiceBuildSdk.signAndStoreDeviceSn(deviceType, sn) / signDeviceSnAsync so the handshake has an snSignature. deviceType is derived from SN prefix: 881 notepro, 880 notepin, 882 notepins, else note.
nodes.notes: Consistent with frozen record: docs/final-closure-report.md:151-155 ('default host platform-jp.plaud.ai'; gen-key returns the RSA private key, sn-sign returns the signature) and docs/protocol-ledger.md:353-357 (credentials are cloud-issued). Cited, not re-derived. iOS wrappers call only agent.initSDK(userAccessToken:customDomain:) with no repoint, implying the iOS SDK honours customDomain internally (inference, not verified here).

nodes.behavior: Capacitor Android source asserts the on-wire bind token is NOT the deviceToken passed to connectBleDevice; the SDK derives it from the JWT `sub` claim (NiceBuildSdk.parseUserIdFromJWT()), and an empty `sub` aborts the handshake with UUID_IS_EMPTY. Yet every wrapper (and the docs) describe deviceToken=userId as 'what binds the device to the user during the handshake'.

nodes.behavior: Capacitor Android logs the derived bind token and the deviceToken in plaintext to logcat on every connect (Log.i with 'bindToken=' and 'deviceToken='), plus initSDK domain and userId.
nodes.notes: Credential material in device logs; demo code.

nodes.behavior: iOS implementations (all three) gate PlaudDeviceAgent.startScan() on BleAgent.shared.isPoweredOn, polling every 0.3 s up to 60 attempts (~18 s) then emitting scanTimeout {reason:'bluetoothNotPoweredOn'}. Capacitor Android and Flutter Android replicate the poll; RN Android checks adapter.isEnabled once and emits scanTimeout immediately.
nodes.evidence: PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:78-109; PlaudSdkModule.swift:144-171; Flutter PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:130-158; PlaudSdkPlugin.java:236-266; PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:283-319; PlaudSdkModule.kt:159-184
nodes.notes: Divergent RN Android semantics.

nodes.behavior: Permission denial semantics differ per wrapper: Capacitor emits scanTimeout{reason:'permissionDenied'} AND rejects 'Bluetooth permissions denied'; RN rejects ERR_PLAUD_PERMISSIONS (and exposes requestPermissions()); Flutter emits scanTimeout{permissionDenied} and resolves. Permission sets also differ: Capacitor/Flutter request BLUETOOTH_SCAN+CONNECT (API31+) or ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION; RN requests SCAN+CONNECT+FINE+COARSE (API31+) or BLUETOOTH+ADMIN+FINE+COARSE.
nodes.notes: Capacitor also re-checks BLUETOOTH_CONNECT in connectBleDevice because the SDK swallows the SecurityException silently (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:284-309).

nodes.behavior: The scanResult.supportWiFi field has three different semantics on Android: Capacitor = IBleAgent.isSupportWifi() of the currently connected agent (false until connected); RN = constant false; Flutter = (projectCode == 881, i.e. NotePro). iOS always reports BleDevice.supportWiFi from the scan record.
nodes.notes: Flutter's mapping ties project code 881 to NotePro (matches deviceType('881')='notepro').

nodes.behavior: Android BleFile lacks sn/channels/isOgg/duration; wrappers synthesize them: Capacitor from TntAgent statics (isOggAudio, OPUS_CHANNEL) and IBleAgent.getSerialNumber(); RN/Flutter from the last-connected BleDevice (audioChannel, isOggAudio, serialNumber; Flutter also updates connectedSn from bleBind status==0). Duration = BleFile.calculateOpusDuration(size, channels)/1000 (80 bytes per 20 ms frame per channel), over-reports for OGG.
nodes.notes: sessionId is read as long on Android to avoid 32-bit truncation (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:474-484).

nodes.behavior: exportAudio writes to a private dir (iOS Documents/PlaudExports, Android files/PlaudExports), formats pcm|mp3|wav|opus (default mp3), channels default 1; the call's promise stays pending until AudioExportCallback.onComplete/onError; progress via exportProgress {sessionId, progress, message}. Wrappers retain the callback bridge in a Set so it is not deallocated mid-export.
nodes.notes: Flutter Android adds an AtomicBoolean 'replied' guard against double completion.

nodes.behavior: All wrappers map bleConnectState(state) to {connected: state==1, failed: state in {2,-1,-2}, state}; 0 = disconnected. Failures are collapsed by the facade; only Capacitor Android recovers the reason via the transport listener (connectFail reason enum: HANDSHAKE_FAIL, SN_NOT_MATCH, TOKEN_NOT_MARCH, TIME_OUT, BLE_CONNECT_FAILED, RECORDING_NOW, USER_REFUSE, MODE_NOT_MATCH, SSN_FAILED, APP_KEY_NOT_MATCH, SYNC_TIME_FAIL, HANDSHAKE_CMD_SEND_FAIL, UUID_IS_EMPTY).
nodes.notes: Frozen record cross-ref: docs/final-closure-report.md:139 and docs/protocol-ledger.md:1450 record bleConnectState(2) as the empty-token abort path. Cited only.

nodes.behavior: Doc's end-to-end flow: (1) partner token via POST /developer/api/oauth/partner/access-token with Basic base64(client_id:secret_key) -> access_token/refresh_token/expires_in 3600; (2) user token via POST /developer/api/open/partner/users/access-token Bearer partner + {user_id 6-120 chars, expires_in 86400}; (3) bind = device linked to exactly one application, partner/user credentials used for encrypting/decrypting/syncing; (4) sync via BLE or WiFi fast transfer (~10x faster, needs HotSpot entitlement); (5) optional upload via generate-presigned-urls / PUT chunks / complete-upload (Bearer user token); (6) transcription POST/GET with X-Client-Api-Key + X-Client-Id, poll to SUCCESS.
nodes.notes: OFFICIAL_DOC claim. The Next.js demo implements exactly this split server-side (plaud-auth.ts / plaud-transcription.ts).

nodes.behavior: Starter app (plaud-template-app, native iOS) is described as including fast-transfer modal, device detail with battery/charging/firmware, manage-device screen and a firmware-update flow -- i.e. exactly the capabilities the cross-platform wrappers omit.
nodes.notes: Confirms the wrappers are a subset by design.

nodes.text: Why the Android SDK's Partner API Retrofit client hardcodes platform-jp and ignores customDomain (every Android wrapper must call NiceBuildSdk.getPartnerApiManager().updateBaseUrl); iOS wrappers do no repoint, so whether the iOS SDK honours customDomain for gen-key/sn-sign is inferred, not verified (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:170-176; PlaudSdkModule.kt:136-141; docs/final-closure-report.md:153).

Why iOS handles partner-data readiness and SN signing internally while Android leaves both to the caller (asymmetry acknowledged in PlaudSdkPlugin.java:345-359 and PlaudSdkModule.kt:425-432 without explanation).
Whether the on-wire bind token is the deviceToken/userId, the JWT `sub` claim, or the 32-hex handshake token in the frozen ledger -- three descriptions coexist (see contradictions).

Meaning of penState fields (state, privacy, keyState, uDisk, findMyToken, hasSndpKey, deviceAccessToken) -- Flutter treats the payload as an 'informational raw map' (plaud_sdk.dart:64-65); no wrapper or wrapper-doc decodes them.
Meaning of bind.status values: Flutter Android treats status==0 as success for connectedSn (PlaudSdkPlugin.kt:552); nothing in the wrappers or the five docs defines the status enumeration.

connectState numeric codes 2 / -1 / -2 are all labelled 'connection/handshake failure' by every wrapper with no distinction (PlaudSdkPlugin.swift:306); the closure report ties state 2 to the empty-token abort (docs/final-closure-report.md:139) but -1/-2 remain undescribed here.

supportWiFi on Android has three different implementations across the three official wrappers (connected-agent flag / constant false / projectCode==881); the authoritative source for WiFi capability on Android is unresolved.

Whether the Android SDK's BleFile.calculateOggDuration page-geometry parameters are documented anywhere; all Android wrappers over-report OGG durations by design (PlaudSdkPlugin.java:786-801; PlaudSdkModule.kt:458-467).

Why the three iOS framework binaries vendored by the wrappers differ from plaud-sdk-public/sdk/ios/*.framework (sha256 differ) while the Android AAR is byte-identical everywhere -- version/packaging relationship not established.
SN prefix -> device type mapping (881 notepro, 880 notepin, 882 notepins, else note) is asserted by wrapper code only; 'notepins' as a distinct device type is not explained in the five target docs.

Whether Plaud's S3 presigned URLs accept a blank Content-Type header (Capacitor Android sends Content-Type: '' when none supplied, PlaudSdkPlugin.java:593-597) -- stated as SignatureDoesNotMatch avoidance, not verified.

Device-recovery semantics ('is_bind false or null' vs true; GET /sdk/binding) are documented for the native SDK (ios-sdk.md:290-300) but no wrapper exposes recoveryConnectBleDevice; how a wrapper-based partner app recovers a locked device is unaddressed.

web-app-wrapper.md:60-67 instructs `cd nextjs-demo && cp .env.example .env`, but no .env.example (or any .env*) exists anywhere in reference/plaud-org/embedded-capacitor (find returned nothing); nextjs-demo/CLAUDE.md:126 and route comments name the required vars (PLAUD_CLIENT_ID, PLAUD_SECRET_KEY, PLAUD_API_KEY) instead.

Devices are identified by a free-form device_id (MAC-style or 'mobile_001').

Wake-word → agent resolution: a device connection has no agent-id header (conn_from_device); on the first listen/detect the server calls internal GET /devices/{device_id}/agent-by-wake with the wake-word text, sets agent_id and owner_id, else marks need_bind and the audio path short-circuits to check_bind_device. Unauthenticated internal endpoints also return agent config (instruction, voice, language from Fish Audio, greeting only if no messages today, last N rounds of chat).

nodes.behavior: Region mismatch is signalled in-band: HTTP 200 with JSON {status:-302, msg:'user region mismatch', data:{domains:{api:'https://api-xxx.plaud.ai'}}}; clients follow once (riffado caps at 3 redirects) to the returned domain. Envelope convention: status 0 = success, msg, optional request_id.

api.plaud.ai sits behind Cloudflare bot protection: a custom UA ('applaud/x.y.z', Node default 'node') receives 403; clients present desktop Chrome/Safari UAs, and riffado layers full browser client-hint headers (sec-ch-ua, Origin https://web.plaud.ai, Referer https://web.plaud.ai/, sec-fetch-site same-site) and optionally rotates Webshare proxies on 403/407.
nodes.notes: Only edge-hosting evidence for the API; nothing about where the web bundle is hosted.

nodes.behavior: Web app request fingerprint replayed by plaud-api: headers 'app-platform: web', 'edit-from: web', Origin/Referer web.plaud.ai, Authorization 'bearer <jwt>' (lowercase), and a random 'r' query/body parameter added to GET/POST/PATCH (cache-buster). Recordings carry an edit_from field.
nodes.notes: Whether the server requires app-platform/edit-from is UNKNOWN; other clients omit them and still work.

nodes.behavior: Login flow A (OTP): POST /auth/otp-send-code {username:email} → {status:0, token:<otp token>}; POST /auth/otp-login {code, token} → access_token (top-level or data.access_token). plaud-toolkit's plan adds a user_area field to both. Flow B (password): POST /auth/access-token form-urlencoded username/password → {status, access_token, token_type}. Flow C: Google/Apple 'Continue with' accounts are a DIFFERENT identity from the OTP email account (OTP returns a token for an empty shadow account); Google users must set a password via Forgot Password to use flow B.

Every password login mints a new session (JWT 'sid' claim) and the backend evicts older sessions for the account, which logs the phone app out; toolkit therefore caches the token and re-logs in only on 401. Token lifetime: README/plan say ~300 days, but the code comment says Plaud currently issues ~30 days.

Legacy browser persistence: web.plaud.ai stored the long-lived user JWT in localStorage key 'tokenstr' (value 'bearer eyJ…'), under Chrome LevelDB origin prefix '_https://web.plaud.ai'; other keys use a per-user prefix 'PLADU_<email>_…' and 'PLADU_<uid>_bearer <jwt>_welcomeFileShown' (a per-account onboarding flag). riffado instead tells users to copy localStorage 'pld_tokenstr'. Plaud later stopped exposing tokenstr (applaud issue #31).
nodes.notes: Mechanism described only. Reading another user's browser store is out of scope and was not executed.

nodes.behavior: Current first-party model (ported from the RoveNotes Connector): three tokens — UT cookie pld_ut (~1 day) used as Bearer for workspace list + mint; URT cookie pld_urt (~30 days) used to refresh the UT; WT (workspace token) used as Bearer for data endpoints. Cookies are set on host plaud.ai / *.plaud.ai. POST /auth/refresh-user-token with Cookie 'pld_ut=…; pld_urt=…' and body {} returns status 0 and Set-Cookie headers: Max-Age=0 clearers FIRST, real tokens LAST; URT is rotated near expiry so both must be persisted; sometimes only one cookie is set. UT JWT carries claims sid/ut_sid, region, iat, exp, and no email. Windows: sign in at web.plaud.ai then open api.plaud.ai/auth/refresh-user-token in the browser to refresh, copy cookies manually.

Workspace layer: GET /team-app/workspaces/list?need_personal_workspace=true (Bearer UT) → data.workspaces[{workspace_id, member_id, name/workspace_name, role, status, workspace_type ('0' = personal; other = team/shared), region, api_domain, created_at, creator_user_id}]. POST /user-app/auth/workspace/token/{workspace_id} (Bearer UT, body {}) → data{workspace_token, expires_in, wt_expires_at, refresh_token, refresh_expires_in, refresh_expires_at, workspace_id, member_id, role}. WT JWT claims ut_ref, wid, wtype; ~24 h. web.plaud.ai puts the WT on /device/list and /file/simple/web. On regional servers, recording endpoints called with a UT instead of a WT return EMPTY lists. 401 on mint = UT dead; other 4xx = stale workspace id (relist). riffado falls back to the UT if mint fails.
nodes.notes: Team workspace CONTENT endpoints (members, shared recordings) are not observed anywhere.

nodes.behavior: GET /user/me → {status, data_user:{id, nickname, email, country}, data_state:{membership_type}}; accepted with a WT as Bearer. riffado's parser guesses email/data.email instead.
nodes.notes: membership_type is the only subscription/entitlement signal on any web endpoint; its value set is UNKNOWN.

nodes.behavior: GET /device/list → {status, data_devices:[{sn, name, model, version_number}]}; used as the connection-validation probe. No bind/unbind/settings/OTA/Wi-Fi operation exists on the web surface in the corpus.

Recording list: GET /file/simple/web?skip&limit&is_trash&sort_by&is_desc → {status, msg, request_id?, data_file_total, data_file_list[]}. is_trash 0 = live, 1 = trash, 2 = all; sort_by start_time|edit_time; riffado uses limit 99999 in one page, applaud pages by 50. Item fields: id, filename, fullname, keywords[], filesize, filetype, file_md5, ori_ready, version, version_ms, edit_time, edit_from, is_trash, start_time/end_time (ms), duration (ms), timezone, zonemins, scene, filetag_id_list[], serial_number, is_trans, is_summary, is_markmemo, wait_pull.
nodes.notes: is_markmemo and wait_pull semantics UNKNOWN (possibly highlight marks / pending device pull).

nodes.behavior: Batch detail: POST /file/list with body = JSON array of file ids → data_file_list[] where each file additionally carries trans_result[] (segments {speaker, content, start_time, end_time}), ai_content (markdown, or a JSON string {markdown} / {content:{markdown}} / {summary}), summary_list[], and extra_data. plaud-api builds transcript, summary, per-recording speaker stats and speaker rename from this.

Per-file manifest: GET /file/detail/{id} → data{file_id, file_name, file_version, duration, is_trash, start_time, scene, serial_number, session_id, filetag_id_list, content_list[{data_id, data_type, task_status (1=ready), err_code, err_msg, data_title, data_tab_name, data_link (presigned S3, body may be gzip)}], embeddings, download_path_mapping, pre_download_content_list[{data_id, data_content (inline JSON string)}], extra_data, has_thought_partner}. Observed data_type/data_id pairs from a captured response: 'transaction' (source_transaction:<hash>:<fid>), 'outline' (source_outline:…), 'auto_sum_note' (auto_sum:…, the primary Summary tab, delivered inline), 'sum_multi_note' (sum_multi:…:<template id>, secondary template notes), 'transaction_polish'. Transcript file named trans_result.json.gz; segments carry speaker and original_speaker. Older recordings keep transcripts only here; newer ones are served by /ai/transsumm.
nodes.notes: data_tab_name implies the web UI renders content items as tabs (Transcript / Summary / Outline / template notes). has_thought_partner and embeddings are unexplained.

nodes.behavior: Transcription job on web: start = PATCH /file/{id} {extra_data:{tranConfig:{language, type_type:'system', type:'REASONING-NOTE', diarization:1, llm:'auto'}}}; poll = POST /ai/transsumm/{id} {is_reload:0, summ_type:'REASONING-NOTE', summ_type_type:'system', info:JSON{language,diarization,llm}, support_mul_summ:true} → {status (plaud-api: 0 'task processing', 1 'task complete', also -111 'success'), data_result[] transcript, data_result_summ (JSON string or object), data_result_summ_mul, outline_result[{start_time,end_time,topic}], outline_task_status, task_id_info, data_source_result, data_note_result, download_link_map, file_version, auto_save, ppc_status, err_code, err_msg}; persist = PATCH /file/{id} {trans_result, ai_content, outline_result, support_mul_summ, extra_data:{task_id_info, aiContentHeader}}. applaud calls transsumm with body {} purely as a read. Long recordings take up to ~10 min.
nodes.notes: 'REASONING-NOTE' with summ_type_type 'system' is the only template identifier seen; a template catalogue endpoint is not observed. Whether the client-side save_results step is truly required or the web app does it is UNKNOWN (plaud-api asserts it).

nodes.behavior: Audio download: GET /file/temp-url/{id}?is_opus=0|1 → {status, temp_url, temp_url_opus?} presigned S3 URLs fetched without auth; GET /file/download/{id} (Bearer) streams directly. Cloud files are labelled .mp3 / audio/mpeg but bytes are Ogg/Opus with vendor tag PALUD.AI (frozen baseline: cloud re-tags/transcodes; not the SDK writer's TinnoTech vendor).

Web upload (scene 101): POST /file/get_upload_presigned_url {filesize, file_type:'MP3'|'OPUS'} → data{part_urls[], upload_id, object_name}; PUT part to S3 (Content-Type application/octet-stream, ETag captured); POST /file/merge_multipart {upload_id, object_name, parts:[{Etag, PartNumber}]}; POST /file/confirm_upload {upload_id, object_name, scene:101, is_tmp:0, support_mul_summ:true, file_type, filename, start_time(ms), session_id(s), serial_number:<uuid4>} → data = Recording.
nodes.notes: serial_number = random uuid suggests uploads impersonate a virtual device; scene 101 meaning INFERRED (web import).

nodes.behavior: Mutations via PATCH /file/{id}: {filename} rename (riffado; note edit_from will be 'web'); {is_trash:true} trash, with a POST /file/trash {file_ids:[…]} fallback that is unverified; {trans_result} speaker rename (client rewrites segment.speaker then PATCHes).

Tags/folders: GET /filetag/ → data_filetag_list[{id, name, file_count}]; membership is only readable via filetag_id_list on each file (client filters the full list). Speakers: GET /speaker/list → data_speaker_list[{id, name, embedding[]}] (global voice-ID list); /speaker/sync path is declared but never called.
nodes.notes: No tag create/assign, no global speaker rename, no /speaker/sync body observed.

nodes.behavior: How third parties model sync (not Plaud behaviour): poll /file/simple/web every 5-10 min, download audio, then transcript+summary once is_trans/is_summary or task_status=1; riffado rate-limits its own /api/plaud/sync per user and retries Plaud 429 honouring Retry-After and 5xx with exponential backoff.

Product operations exposed by community MCP/CLI/skills (a proxy for what users do on web): list recordings, get transcript, get recording detail, user info, temp MP3 URL (toolkit MCP); upload+analyze, transcription start/status/get/summary, download, speakers list/recording/rename, tags list/recordings, auth setup (plaud-api CLI + Claude skill).

nodes.behavior: OTA mechanism in the prototype is upstream xiaozhi's: HTTP POST to OTA_URL with headers Activation-Version (1 or 2 depending on efuse serial), Device-Id (MAC), Client-Id (board UUID), Serial-Number (efuse USER_DATA), User-Agent; response JSON {firmware:{version,url}, activation:{code,challenge,message,timeout_ms}, ...}; upgrade streams url into the next OTA slot via esp_ota_begin/esp_ota_write/esp_ota_end/esp_ota_set_boot_partition; activation answers the challenge with hmac-sha256 over efuse HMAC_KEY0. No custom image format, no esp_https_ota component.
nodes.notes: Identical mechanism to upstream; Plaud only changed the URL.

nodes.behavior: BLE push protocol driven by sdk.ble.util.SimpleFirmwareTransfer: computes CRC-16 of the file (proto.t0.a), sends a 'firmware push' command built by proto.i(long uid, String fromVersion, String toVersion, int thirdVersion, long fileSize, int crc).enPkg() as opcode 50 registered with expected response opcodes {50, 52}; the device then requests data ranges (52, 'received data packet request', '到达请求边界 start/end'), the phone sends packets with retry, and the device ends with 51 (verified as u16le at offset 1 via TntBleCommUtils.b, data length >= 7) carrying a status byte; phone sends sendFotaComplete(uid, status) and enters DEVICE_RESTARTING → RECONNECTING_DEVICE → WAITING_UPGRADE_RESULT. Status decode: 0 Success, 1 Upgrade failed, 2 Version mismatch, 3 Flash write failed, 4 File too large, 5 Too many attempts, 6 Device is in USB drive mode, 7 Device is recording, 8 Not enough space, 9 Device is busy, 10 G101 glasses: upgrade only while charging, 11 G101 glasses: battery too low, 12 G101 glasses: switching to OTA_MODE; also 'Wrong device mode (recorder is not in recording mode)'.
nodes.evidence: build/evidence/javap/ALL.txt:125590-128653 (class span); status tableswitch and strings at process_item_data(int) (ldc 'Success'…'Wrong device mode'); opcode constants bipush 50/52 at ~:128591 with '【阶段2-推送】发送固件推送命令' and proto.i.<init>(JLjava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;IJI)V; bipush 51 / bipush 7 / TntBleCommUtils.b at ~:127165 with '【命令验证】期望命令类型'; '【阶段2-CRC】CRC-16: 0x%04X' ; 'sendFotaComplete:(II)V'; enum com.plaud.sdk.proto.s0$i (:54569) with OTA_PUSH_ERROR_G101_POWER_LOW / _NO_CHARGING / _MODE_TRANS
nodes.notes: Opcode numbering (50/51/52) is read from bipush constants adjacent to the send/verify calls; the ledger's opcode table (§5) does not list them, so wire layout beyond 'type-1 frame, u16le opcode at offset 1' is not re-derived here. Matches iOS header cmd docs: pushFotaInfo → callbacks bleFotaPackReq / bleFotaResult.

nodes.behavior: Official iOS header documents the same OTA contract: pushFotaInfo(uid, fromVersion 'T0012'/'V0012', toVersion, thirdVersion ('G101 project, else 0'), fileSize bytes, crc) with a typed overload adding fromVersionType/toVersionType and 'target version must exceed current'; device→phone bleSyncOtaFileInfo (cmd 151: uid, start, end, toVersion, toVersionType, isSilent, packetCheckOk); OTA result status list identical to the Android decode plus 13 = 'silent OTA transfer succeeded (firmware received, upgrade on next reboot)' and 255 = 'wrong mode (recording pen not in recording mode, specific to Heili three-way switch)'; errmsg returns the post-upgrade version on protocol version 4.
nodes.notes: Version strings 'T0012'/'V0012' = versionType letter + numeric code; Android template validates '^[VT]\d+$' (DeviceManager.kt:575-577).

nodes.behavior: Cloud version check (template implementation, mirrors iOS SDK): GET {platformHost}/developer/api/open/partner/sdk/version/latest?type=<notepro|notepin|notepins|note>&sn=<SN>&current_version=-1 with header X-Device-Signature (the sn-sign signature); response JSON version_code, download_url, version_type, version_number, version_description, is_force, is_strong_guidance, file_md5; hasUpdate = version_code > device code && download_url non-empty. The AAR's own checkFirmwareUpdate needs an internal sdkToken from /api/oauth/sdk-token which the developer platform does not serve (404 per the template comment), so the template bypasses it. DeviceVersionResponse model: type, model, versionType, versionCode, versionNumber, versionDescription, downloadUrl (+isForce, isStrongGuidance, fileMd5 per constructor use).

'G101 glasses' product code with charging-only/low-battery/OTA_MODE rules and a dedicated 'thirdVersion' OTA field (javap SimpleFirmwareTransfer strings; PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:766,1395): no other source describes the device, its radio platform, or its firmware.
'Heili (黑黎) three-way switch' recording pen behind OTA status 255 'not in recording mode' (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1395): unnamed elsewhere; unclear whether it is a Plaud SKU or a Tinno platform sibling.

OTA status 13 'silent OTA transfer succeeded, upgrade on next reboot' exists only in the newer iOS header (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:2241) and in bleSyncOtaFileInfo's isSilent flag (:1442); the Android bytecode status switch covers 0-12 only, so how the Android SDK handles a silent-OTA device is unknown.

Device status bit6 'pan上云' (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1437) — the meaning of 'pan' (network drive? partner?) and the upload path are unexplained; bit5 Wi-Fi cloud upload and its domain/IP setter (dataType 1, :922-929) imply direct device-to-cloud upload that no client in the corpus exercises.

The xiaozhi prototype's server pair sits on private LAN IP 10.1.164.12 (ports 8000/8002); which live-agent deployment/agent it targeted, and whether 'hi plaud' devices were ever provisioned against production, is unknown.

client-sdk-esp32's dynamic-token demo names a 'hospital_assistant' agent with role metadata (voice_agent/sdkconfig:610-611); no corpus source explains the scenario or its relationship to any Plaud product.

The 'sdkconfig.backup.wrong_board_20251010_181726' file shows an earlier build against bread-compact-wifi with an SSD1306 OLED; whether custom Plaud hardware was ever targeted (rather than dev kits) cannot be determined — no Plaud board directory exists in either fork.

The xiaozhi OTA endpoint's activation flow (efuse serial + HMAC_KEY0 challenge, main/ota.cc:409-431) is upstream code; whether Plaud's live-agent fork actually issues activation challenges to 'hi plaud' devices is not visible from the device side.

Wi-Fi OTA (device status bit8, PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:1438) vs the ledger's phone-hosted WebSocket OTA message types 20-22: which side downloads the image in the Wi-Fi path (device from cloud, or phone pushing) is not established by any source.

Silent OTA: iOS header (newer build) documents status 13 'silent OTA transfer succeeded' and an isSilent flag (PlaudBleSDK-Swift.h:2241, 1442); the Android AAR's status decoder stops at 12 (javap tableswitch 0..12) — SDK generations diverge.

Version check ownership: the AAR exposes FirmwareUpdateManager.checkForUpdate (javap :91613ff) but the official Android template says it cannot work through the GA facade (needs /api/oauth/sdk-token, 404 on platform-us) and re-implements the check app-side (DeviceManager.kt:523-530) — SDK claims a capability the published platform does not serve.

Wake-word threshold: sdkconfig:716 says CONFIG_CUSTOM_WAKE_WORD_THRESHOLD=50 (0.5) and Kconfig help says default 20, but the compiled code ignores the macro and hard-codes 0.15 (custom_wake_word.cc:98) while the uncompiled multinet_only variant uses 0.5 (custom_wake_word_multinet_only.cc:98).

Delta manifest vs content: the manifest's 376 'only-in-Plaud' paths suggest large Plaud additions, but content shows ~350 of them are upstream v2.0.x files that upstream v2.5.0 relocated under vendor directories; the true Plaud delta is <10 files.

README of client-sdk-esp32 fork advertises livekit 0.3.0 and lacks the upstream 0.3.11 custom_hardware (ES8311+ES7210) example, so the fork predates the very example that would have been the natural base for custom hardware.

nodes.claim: The Plaud device is ESP32-class
nodes.evidence: For the BLE recorder (Note Pro 881 / NotePin S 882 / NotePin 880 / Note 888): ledger §1.4 and closure report identify a TinnoTech Pen BLE platform; AAR native libs contain only TinnoTech JNI symbols and no ESP/OTA-image strings (build/evidence/aar/jni/*/libtnt_ble_utils.so, libjni_ogg.so); the two ESP32 forks contain zero Tinno/881/NotePin strings and compile Bluetooth out (xiaozhi sdkconfig:1068), so they cannot be the 1910-service recorder. The forks target Espressif Korvo dev kits (xiaozhi sdkconfig:633; client-sdk voice_agent/sdkconfig:602). Whether some other Plaud line (e.g. the 'G101 glasses' seen only in OTA status strings) is ESP32-class is UNVERIFIABLE from the corpus.

nodes.claim: xiaozhi-esp32 is Plaud's reference firmware
nodes.evidence: It is a Plaud engineer's prototyping snapshot of upstream xiaozhi-esp32 v2.0.3 (CMakeLists.txt:7) with a 'hi plaud' MultiNet wake word (custom_wake_word.cc:91-126, sdkconfig:713-716) and LAN defaults pointing at Plaud's live-agent server fork (Kconfig.projbuild:3-5, websocket_protocol.cc:93; live-agent/README.md:21-22). That makes it reference/prototype firmware for a Wi-Fi voice-agent companion, not for any shipped recorder: no Plaud board definition, no Plaud pin map, no product-name strings, dev-kit hardware only, debug-level thresholds (0.15 'maximum sensitivity testing'). It does not describe the Note Pro/NotePin S firmware.

nodes.behavior: Docs list `bleState(powered: Bool)` as a PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol callback ('Phone Bluetooth power state') but the protocol in the binary has no such member. PlaudDeviceAgent implements BleAgentProtocol.bleState internally but cannot forward it to an app delegate because the app-facing protocol lacks the selector.
nodes.evidence: IOS:225, IOS:803 (doc tables) vs BASIC:1152-1203 (full PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol, no bleState) and BASIC:1340 (facade's own BleAgentProtocol conformance has bleState)
nodes.notes: App must drop to BleAgent.isPoweredOn (BLE:207) or its own CBCentralManager to observe radio state.

nodes.behavior: Doc counts are exact: BleAgentProtocol = 96 required `@objc func` + 1 `@objc optional` (bleConnectStage) = 97; PlaudDeviceAgentProtocol = 1 required (blePenState) + 49 optional; PlaudWiFiAgentProtocol = 21 members, all optional; low-level WiFiAgentProtocol = 19 required + 2 optional (wifiConnected, onWiFiConnectStateChanged).
